sentences.zh: 李雄

translations.literal: Li Xiong
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong

sentences.zh: 李雄，字仲俊，特第三子也。

translations.literal: Li Xiong, courtesy name Zhongjun, was the third son of Li Te.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong, whose courtesy name was Zhongjun, was the third son of Li Te.

sentences.zh: 母羅氏，夢雙虹自門升天，一虹中斷，既而生蕩。

translations.literal: His mother, the Lady Luo, dreamed that twin rainbows rose from the gate to heaven; one rainbow broke in the middle, and afterward she gave birth to Dang.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Luo, dreamed of twin rainbows climbing from the gate toward the sky; one snapped midway, and she thereafter bore Li Dang.

sentences.zh: 後羅氏因汲水，忽然如寐，又夢大蛇繞其身，遂有孕，十四月而生雄。

translations.literal: Later the Lady Luo, while drawing water, suddenly seemed to fall asleep; she again dreamed a great serpent coiled around her body, and she thereupon became pregnant, and after fourteen months gave birth to Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while Lady Luo was drawing water, she suddenly slipped into something like sleep and dreamed a great snake coiled about her; she conceived, and after fourteen months she gave birth to Li Xiong.

sentences.zh: 常言吾二子若有先亡，在者必大貴。

translations.literal: She often said, "If among my two sons one dies first, the one who remains will surely be greatly honored."
translations.idiomatic: She would often say that if one of her two sons died first, the survivor was destined for greatness.

sentences.zh: 蕩竟前死。

translations.literal: Dang in the end died before.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dang ended up dying first.

sentences.zh: 雄身長八尺三寸，美容貌。

translations.literal: Xiong's body was eight chi and three cun in height, and he had handsome features.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong stood eight chi and three cun tall and was strikingly good-looking.

sentences.zh: 少以烈氣聞，每周旋鄉里，識達之士皆器重之。

translations.literal: In youth he was known for fierce spirit; whenever he moved about the countryside, knowledgeable and discerning gentlemen all esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was known for his fierce mettle, and whenever he passed through the local communities, men of insight treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 有劉化者，道術士也，每謂人曰：「關、隴之士皆當南移，李氏子中惟仲俊有奇表，終為人主。」

translations.literal: There was one Liu Hua, a Daoist adept, who often said to people, "The gentlemen of Guan and Long will all shift southward; among the sons of the Li clan only Zhongjun has a marvelous appearance, and in the end he will become a ruler."
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist named Liu Hua was fond of telling people that the elite of the Guan and Long regions would drift southward, and that among Li Te’s sons only Zhongjun bore the portents of a future sovereign.

sentences.zh: 特起兵於蜀，承制，以雄為前將軍。

translations.literal: Te raised troops in Shu, acting on delegated authority, and appointed Xiong as Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Te rose in Shu under plenipotentiary orders from the court, he named Li Xiong Forward General.

sentences.zh: 流死，雄自稱大都督、大將軍、益州牧，都於郫城。

translations.literal: Liu died; Xiong styled himself Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, and Governor of Yi Province, and made his capital at Pi.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Liu died, Li Xiong took the titles of grand commander-in-chief, grand general, and shepherd of Yi Province, and fixed his seat at Pi.

sentences.zh: 羅尚遣將攻雄，雄擊走之。

translations.literal: Luo Shang sent generals to attack Xiong; Xiong struck them and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang sent generals against him; Li Xiong routed their forces.

sentences.zh: 李驤攻犍為，斷尚運道，尚軍大餒，攻之又急，遂留牙門羅特固守，尚委城夜遁。

translations.literal: Li Xiang attacked Qianwei, cut off Shang's supply routes, and Shang's army greatly starved; the attacks were again pressing, so he left Ya-men Luo Te to hold firm, and Shang abandoned the city and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang struck Qianwei and severed Luo Shang’s supply lines until his troops were starving; pressed by relentless assaults, Luo Shang left the garrison commander Luo Te to hold the line and slipped out of the city under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 特開門內雄，遂克成都。

translations.literal: Te opened the gates to admit Xiong, and they thereupon took Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Te opened the gates to Li Xiong, and Chengdu fell.

sentences.zh: 于時雄軍饑甚，乃率眾就谷於郪，掘野芋而食之。

translations.literal: At that time Xiong's army was extremely hungry, so he led the multitude to seek grain at Qi, dug wild taro, and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong’s army was starving, so he marched his men to Qi for food and lived on wild taro they dug from the fields.

sentences.zh: 蜀人流散，東下江陽，南入七郡。

translations.literal: The people of Shu scattered, eastward down to Jiangyang, southward into the seven commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu populace fled in all directions—east toward Jiangyang and south into the seven southern commanderies.

sentences.zh: 雄以西山范長生岩居穴處，求道養志，欲迎立為君而臣之。

translations.literal: Xiong, because Fan Changsheng of the Western Hills dwelt in cliffs and caves, seeking the Way and nurturing his will, wished to welcome and establish him as ruler and himself be his subject.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Changsheng of the Western Hills lived as a recluse in mountain caves, cultivating the Way; Li Xiong wanted to install him as sovereign and serve him as a subject.

sentences.zh: 長生固辭。

translations.literal: Changsheng firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Changsheng firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 雄乃深自挹損，不敢稱制，事無巨細，皆決于李國、李離兄弟。

translations.literal: Xiong thereupon deeply restrained himself, did not dare assume imperial authority, and in affairs whether great or small all was decided by the brothers Li Guo and Li Li.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong therefore held himself in check, avoided claiming supreme authority, and left every decision, large or small, to Li Guo and Li Li.

sentences.zh: 國等事雄彌謹。

translations.literal: Guo and the others served Xiong ever more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guo and his circle only grew more scrupulous in serving Li Xiong.

sentences.zh: 諸將固請雄即尊位，以僭稱成都王，赦其境內，建元為建興，除晉法，約法七章。

translations.literal: The generals firmly requested Xiong to assume the exalted position; he usurpingly styled himself King of Chengdu, amnestied his territory, established the era name Jianxing, abolished Jin law, and made a compact of seven articles of law.
translations.idiomatic: His generals pressed him to take the throne; he assumed the title King of Chengdu, proclaimed an amnesty, adopted the reign title Jianxing, discarded Jin statutes, and promulgated a seven-article legal code.

sentences.zh: 以其叔父驤為太傅，兄始為太保，折沖李離為太尉，建威李雲為司徙，翊軍李璜為司空，材官李國為太宰，其餘拜授各有差。

translations.literal: He appointed his uncle Xiang as Grand Tutor, elder brother Shi as Grand Guardian, Li Li, General Who Repels Assaults, as Grand Commandant, Li Yun, General Who Establishes Might, as Minister over the Masses, Li Huang, General Who Aids the Army, as Minister of Works, Li Guo, Material Officer, as Grand Minister; the rest received appointments each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He named his uncle Li Xiang grand tutor, his elder brother Li Shi grand guardian, Li Li grand commandant with the title “General Who Repels Assaults,” Li Yun minister over the masses with the title “General Who Establishes Might,” Li Huang minister of works as “General Who Aids the Army,” and Li Guo grand minister; other officers received posts commensurate with their station.

sentences.zh: 追尊其曾祖武曰巴郡桓公，祖慕隴西襄王，父特成都景王，母羅氏曰王太后。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his great-grandfather Wu as Duke Huan of Bajun, grandfather Mu as Prince Xiang of Longxi, father Te as Prince Jing of Chengdu, and mother the Lady Luo as Queen Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously ennobled his great-grandfather Wu as Duke Huan of Ba commandery, his grandfather Mu as Prince Xiang of Longxi, his father Li Te as Prince Jing of Chengdu, and his mother Lady Luo as queen dowager.

sentences.zh: 范長生自西山乘素輿詣成都，雄迎之於門，執版延坐，拜丞相，尊曰範賢。

translations.literal: Fan Changsheng from the Western Hills rode a plain palanquin to Chengdu; Xiong welcomed him at the gate, grasping a tablet and inviting him to sit, appointed him Chancellor, and honored him as Fan the Worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Changsheng came down from the Western Hills in a plain litter; Li Xiong met him at the gate, conducted him inside with formal tablet in hand, named him chancellor, and styled him “Fan the Worthy.”

sentences.zh: 長生勸雄稱尊號，雄於是僭即帝位，赦其境內，改年曰太武。

translations.literal: Changsheng urged Xiong to assume the exalted title; Xiong thereupon usurpingly ascended the imperial throne, amnestied his territory, and changed the year to Taiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Changsheng urged him to take the imperial title; Li Xiong then proclaimed himself emperor, issued an amnesty, and adopted the reign name Taiwu.

sentences.zh: 追尊父特曰景帝，廟號始祖，母羅氏為太后。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his father Te as Emperor Jing, temple name First Ancestor, and the Lady Luo as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He canonized his father Li Te as Emperor Jing with the temple epithet First Ancestor and elevated Lady Luo to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 加范長生為天地太師，封西山侯，復其部曲不豫軍征，租稅一入其家。

translations.literal: He added to Fan Changsheng the title Grand Preceptor of Heaven and Earth, enfeoffed him as Marquis of the Western Hills, exempted his personal following from military levies, and had all rent and tax revenue go to his household.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed on Fan Changsheng the title grand preceptor of heaven and earth, made him marquis of the Western Hills, excused his retainers from conscription, and diverted the taxes of his domain straight into Fan’s household.

sentences.zh: 雄時建國草創，素無法式，諸將恃恩，各爭班位。

translations.literal: At the time Xiong was founding the state in haste; there had never been statutes or models, and the generals relied on favor, each contending for order of precedence.
translations.idiomatic: The new state was still being improvised, with no settled institutions, and commanders jostled for rank, each trading on past favors.

sentences.zh: 其尚書令閻式上疏曰：「夫為國制法，勳尚仍舊。

translations.literal: His Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Yan Shi, submitted a memorial saying, "In making laws for the state, merit honors should follow precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi, director of the secretariat, memorialized: “When a state frames its laws, rewards for merit must rest on precedent.

sentences.zh: 漢、晉故事，惟太尉、大司馬執兵，太傅、太保父兄之官，論道之職，司徙、司空掌五教九土之差。

translations.literal: By Han and Jin precedent, only the Grand Commandant and Grand Marshal hold military power; the Grand Tutor and Grand Guardian are offices of fathers and elder brothers, posts for discussing the Way; the Minister over the Masses and Minister of Works administer the distinctions of the five teachings and the nine soils.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han and Jin precedent, only the grand commandant and grand marshal wielded arms; the grand tutor and grand guardian were honorific “elder kinsman” posts devoted to counsel; the ministers over the masses and of works oversaw civil order and territorial administration.

sentences.zh: 秦置丞相，總領萬機。

translations.literal: Qin established the chancellor, who overall directed the myriad threads.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin had created the chancellor to manage every branch of government.

sentences.zh: 漢武之末，越以大將軍統政。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Wu of Han's reign, Guang, as grand general, directed government.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Emperor Wu of Han’s reign, Huo Guang was governing the realm in the capacity of grand general.

sentences.zh: 今國業初建，凡百末備，諸公大將班位有差，降而兢請施置，不與典故相應，宜立制度以為楷式。

translations.literal: Now the state enterprise is newly founded; the hundred affairs are not yet prepared; the dukes and great generals have differences in order of rank; descending, they eagerly request appointments and arrangements; it does not correspond to classical models—it is fitting to establish institutions to serve as a standard pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Our polity is brand-new and nothing is yet in place; senior ministers and generals already differ in seniority, yet offices are being handed out piecemeal without regard to classical precedent. We should codify ranks and duties into a clear model.”

sentences.zh: 」雄從之。

translations.literal: " Xiong followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 遣李國、李雲等率眾二萬寇漢中，梁州刺史張殷奔于長安。

translations.literal: He sent Li Guo, Li Yun, and others to lead a host of twenty thousand to raid Hanzhong; the Inspector of Liang Province, Zhang Yin, fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Li Guo and Li Yun with twenty thousand men against Hanzhong, driving Inspector Zhang Yin of Liang province to flee to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 國等陷南鄭，盡徙漢中人於蜀。

translations.literal: Guo and the others took Nan Zheng and entirely moved the people of Hanzhong into Shu.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Nan Zheng and deported the entire population of Hanzhong into Shu.

sentences.zh: 先是，南土頻歲饑疫，死者十萬計。

translations.literal: Before this, the southern lands for successive years had famine and pestilence; the dead were counted in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: For years the south had suffered famine and plague; deaths ran into the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 南夷校尉李毅固守不降，雄誘建寧夷使討之。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Southern Yi, Li Yi, held firm and did not submit; Xiong enticed the Jianning Yi to send forces against him.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Li Yi of the southern tribes refused to yield, so Li Xiong incited the Jianning tribesmen to attack him.

sentences.zh: 毅病卒，城陷，殺壯士三千餘人，送婦女千口于成都。

translations.literal: Yi fell ill and died; the city fell; they killed more than three thousand stalwarts and sent a thousand women to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yi died of illness the city fell; over three thousand defenders were slaughtered, and a thousand women were marched to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 時李離據梓潼，其部將羅羕、張金苟等殺離及閻式，以梓潼歸於羅尚。

translations.literal: At the time Li Li held Zitong; his subordinate generals Luo Yan, Zhang Jingou, and others killed Li and Yan Shi, and gave Zitong to Luo Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Li held Zitong until his officers Luo Yan and Zhang Jingou murdered him and Yan Shi and handed the city to Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 尚遣其將向奮屯安漢之宜福以逼雄，雄率眾攻奮，不克。

translations.literal: Shang sent his general Xiang Fen to encamp at Yifu in Anhan to press Xiong; Xiong led the host to attack Fen but did not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang stationed Xiang Fen at Yifu in Anhan to threaten Li Xiong, who attacked him without success.

sentences.zh: 時李國鎮巴西，其帳下文碩又殺國，以巴西降尚。

translations.literal: At the time Li Guo garrisoned Baxi; his clerk Wen Shuo again killed Guo and surrendered Baxi to Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guo was holding Baxi when his aide Wen Shuo assassinated him and surrendered the commandery to Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 雄乃引還，遣其將張寶襲梓潼，陷之。

translations.literal: Xiong thereupon led back, sent his general Zhang Bao to raid Zitong, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong withdrew, then sent Zhang Bao on a surprise attack that retook Zitong.

sentences.zh: 會羅尚卒，巴郡亂，李驤攻涪，又陷之，執梓潼太守譙登，遂乘勝進軍討文碩，害之。

translations.literal: When Luo Shang died, Baxi was in turmoil; Li Xiang attacked Fu and again took it, seized the Administrator of Zitong, Qiao Deng, then rode victory to advance the army against Wen Shuo and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang’s death threw Ba commandery into chaos; Li Xiang seized Fu, captured Zitong’s governor Qiao Deng, then pressed on and executed Wen Shuo.

sentences.zh: 雄大悅，赦其境內，改元曰玉衡。

translations.literal: Xiong was greatly pleased, amnestied his territory, and changed the era name to Yuheng.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Li Xiong proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the reign title Yuheng.

sentences.zh: 雄母羅氏死，雄信巫覡者之言，多有忌諱，至欲不葬。

translations.literal: Xiong's mother the Lady Luo died; Xiong believed the words of shamans and had many taboos, to the point of wishing not to bury her.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Luo died, Li Xiong heeded spirit mediums and became so obsessed with taboos that he nearly refused her burial.

sentences.zh: 其司空趙肅諫，雄乃從之。

translations.literal: His Minister of Works Zhao Su remonstrated, and Xiong then followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhao Su talked him out of it, and Li Xiong relented.

sentences.zh: 雄欲申三年之禮，群臣固諫，雄弗許。

translations.literal: Xiong wished to extend the three-year rites; the host of ministers firmly remonstrated; Xiong did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong meant to observe the full three-year mourning; his ministers protested vigorously, but he would not bend.

sentences.zh: 李驤謂司空上官惇曰：「今方難未弭，吾欲固諫，不聽主上終諒闇，君以為何如？

translations.literal: Li Xiang said to Minister of Works Shangguan Dun, "Now the difficulties are not yet quelled; I wish firmly to remonstrate; if he does not listen, the ruler will in the end observe full mourning seclusion—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang said to Minister of Works Shangguan Dun, “The realm is still unsettled. I mean to press the issue: if he refuses to listen, the sovereign will sit out the entire mourning seclusion. What is your view?”

sentences.zh: 」惇曰：「三年之喪，自天子達于庶人，故孔子曰：'何必高宗，古之人皆然。

translations.literal: " Dun said, "The three-year mourning, from the Son of Heaven reaching to the common people—therefore Confucius said, 'Why only Gaozong—the ancients were all thus.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Dun replied, “The three-year mourning obligation runs from the Son of Heaven down to the commoner; Confucius said, ‘It was not only Gaozong—the ancients all did this.’”

sentences.zh: '但漢、魏以來，天下多難，宗廟至重，不可久曠，故釋衰絰，至哀而已。

translations.literal: ' But from Han and Wei onward, the realm has had many difficulties; the ancestral temple is supremely weighty and cannot long be left vacant; therefore they put off hemp mourning garments—only the utmost grief.
translations.idiomatic: “Yet since Han and Wei times the empire has known endless crises; the ancestral cult cannot be left unattended, so rulers set aside sackcloth after expressing the depth of their grief.”

sentences.zh: 」驤曰：「任回方至，此人決於行事，且上常難達違言，待其至，當與俱請。

translations.literal: " Xiang said, "Ren Hui is about to arrive; this man is decisive in action; moreover the sovereign often finds it hard to reject contrary words; when he arrives, I shall with him together request.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang answered, “Ren Hui is due soon—he is forceful in counsel, and the throne seldom brushes aside blunt advice. When he arrives we should petition together.”

sentences.zh: 」及回至，驤與回俱見雄。

translations.literal: " When Hui arrived, Xiang and Hui together had audience with Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Hui arrived, he and Li Xiang were admitted to an audience with Li Xiong.

sentences.zh: 驤免冠流涕，固請公除。

translations.literal: Xiang removed cap and wept, firmly requesting public removal of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang doffed his cap and wept as he begged the sovereign to accept formal dismissal of mourning.

sentences.zh: 雄號泣不許。

translations.literal: Xiong wailed and wept and did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong sobbed and refused.

sentences.zh: 回跪而進曰：「今王業初建，凡百草創，一日無主，天下惶惶。

translations.literal: Hui knelt and advanced saying, "Now the royal enterprise is newly founded; the hundred grass-roots are in creation; one day without a ruler, the realm is fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Hui knelt forward and said, “The dynasty is new and everything is improvised; a single day without a sovereign leaves the realm adrift.”

sentences.zh: 昔武王素甲觀兵，晉襄墨絰從戎，豈所願哉？

translations.literal: Formerly King Wu in plain armor reviewed the troops; Jin Xiang in ink hemp followed the army—was it what they wished?
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou reviewed his hosts in undyed armor; Duke Wen of Jin went to war in ink-stained mourning—do you think they wanted to?”

sentences.zh: 為天下屈己故也。

translations.literal: It was for the realm bending themselves thus.
translations.idiomatic: They humbled themselves for the sake of the world.”

sentences.zh: 願陛下割情從權，永隆天保。

translations.literal: We hope Your Majesty will cut emotion and follow expedient, forever prospering Heaven's protection.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to set private feeling aside for the exigency of state and so secure the mandate long into the future.”

sentences.zh: 」遂強扶雄起，釋服親政。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they forcibly helped Xiong rise, put off garments, and personally administered government.
translations.idiomatic: They lifted him to his feet, helped him out of mourning dress, and returned him to active rule.

sentences.zh: 是時南得漢嘉、涪陵，遠人繼至，雄於是下寬大之令，降附者皆假復除。

translations.literal: At this time in the south they had obtained Hanjia and Fuling; distant people came in succession; Xiong thereupon issued lenient and broad orders; those who surrendered and attached were all granted temporary exemption and removal of obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Hanja and Fuling had fallen to the south and refugees kept arriving; Li Xiong issued generous terms, granting tax relief and amnesty to everyone who submitted.

sentences.zh: 虛己愛人，授用皆得其才，益州遂定。

translations.literal: He emptied himself and loved people; appointments and employments all obtained their talent; Yi Province was thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: He listened to others and cared for his people, placed every man according to his ability, and Yi province gradually stabilized.

sentences.zh: 偽立其妻任氏為皇后。

translations.literal: Falsely he established his wife the Lady Ren as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He named his wife Lady Ren empress of his new dynasty.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊難敵兄弟為劉曜所破，奔葭萌，遣子入質。

translations.literal: The Di king Yang Nan-di and his brothers were broken by Liu Yao; they fled to Jiameng and sent sons as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Yang Nan-di and his kinsmen, routed by Liu Yao, fled to Jiameng and sent hostages—sons of the leading houses—to Li Xiong’s court.

sentences.zh: 隴西賊帥陳安又附之。

translations.literal: The Longxi bandit chief Chen An again attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An, the rebel leader of Longxi, also threw in his lot with him.

sentences.zh: 遣李驤征越巂，太守李釗降。

translations.literal: He sent Li Xiang to campaign against Yuexi; the Administrator Li Zhao surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Xiang against Yuexi; Governor Li Zhao capitulated.

sentences.zh: 驤進軍由小會攻甯州刺史王遜，遜使其將姚嶽悉眾距戰。

translations.literal: Xiang advanced the army by Xiaohui to attack Inspector of Ning Province Wang Xun; Xun sent his general Yao Yue with the full host to resist battle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang pushed through Xiaohui to strike Wang Xun, inspector of Ning province, who sent Yao Yue with every available man to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 驤軍不利，又遇霖雨，驤引軍還，爭濟瀘水，士眾多死。

translations.literal: Xiang's army was not favorable; again they encountered long rain; Xiang led the army back; contending to cross the Lu River, soldiers and multitude many died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang’s campaign faltered in the monsoon; on the retreat his men stampeded across the Lu River and thousands drowned or were crushed.

sentences.zh: 釗到成都，雄待遇甚厚，朝遷儀式，喪紀之禮，皆決於釗。

translations.literal: When Zhao arrived at Chengdu, Xiong treated him very generously; court-movement ritual forms, mourning rites, all were decided by Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhao arrived in Chengdu, Li Xiong treated him with exceptional honor and entrusted him with court ritual and the full protocol of mourning.

sentences.zh: 楊難敵之奔葭萌也，雄安北李稚厚撫之，縱其兄弟還武都，難敵遂恃險多為不法，稚請討之。

translations.literal: When Yang Nan-di fled to Jiameng, Xiong's Defender of the North Li Zhi generously comforted him, released his brothers to return to Wudu; Nan-di thereupon relied on the passes and did much unlawful conduct; Zhi requested to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Nan-di fled to Jiameng, Li Zhi, Li Xiong’s defender of the north, treated him generously and even let his brothers return to Wudu—whereupon Nan-di abused the mountain defenses and broke every agreement, until Li Zhi asked permission to chastise him.

sentences.zh: 雄遣中領軍琀及將軍樂次、費他、李乾等由白水橋攻下辯，征東李壽督琀弟玝攻陰平。

translations.literal: Xiong sent Central Army Li Han and generals Le Ci, Fei Ta, Li Qian, and others by the White Water Bridge to attack Xia Bian; Li Shou, General Who Conquers the East, supervised Han's younger brother Yu to attack Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong sent Guard General Li Han with Le Ci, Fei Ta, and Li Qian across the White Water Bridge against Xia Bian, while Li Shou, his general conquering the east, directed Li Han’s brother Li Yu against Yinping.

sentences.zh: 難敵遣軍距之，壽不得進，而琀、稚長驅至武街。

translations.literal: Nan-di sent troops to resist them; Shou could not advance, but Han and Zhi long-drove to Wujie.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Nan-di blocked Li Shou, but Li Han and Li Zhi raced ahead as far as Wujie.

sentences.zh: 難敵遣兵斷其歸道，四面攻之，獲琀、稚，死者數千人。

translations.literal: Nan-di sent troops to cut off their return road, attacked them on four sides, captured Han and Zhi; the dead were several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Nan-di severed their line of retreat, surrounded them, and took Li Han and Li Zhi prisoner; several thousand of their soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 琀、稚，雄兄蕩之子也。

translations.literal: Han and Zhi were the sons of Xiong's elder brother Dang.
translations.idiomatic: Both men were nephews of Li Xiong—sons of his brother Li Dang.

sentences.zh: 雄深悼之，不食者數日，言則流涕，深自咎責焉。

translations.literal: Xiong deeply mourned them, for several days not eating; when he spoke he shed tears, deeply blaming himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong grieved so deeply that he fasted for days, wept whenever he spoke of the disaster, and blamed himself harshly.

sentences.zh: 其後將立蕩子班為太子。

translations.literal: Afterward he was about to establish Dang's son Ban as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He later resolved to name Li Dang’s son Li Ban crown prince.

sentences.zh: 雄有子十餘人，群臣咸欲立雄所生。

translations.literal: Xiong had more than ten sons; the host of ministers all wished to establish those born of Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong had more than ten sons of his own, and the ministers wanted one of them named heir.

sentences.zh: 雄曰：「起兵之初，舉手捍頭，本不希帝王之業也。

translations.literal: Xiong said, "At the beginning of raising troops, lifting hand to shield the head, originally I did not hope for the enterprise of emperor and king.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong said, “When we first took up arms we were only shielding our necks—we never aspired to an imperial throne.”

sentences.zh: 值天下喪亂，晉氏播蕩，群情義舉，志濟塗炭，而諸君遂見推逼，處王公之上。

translations.literal: It met the realm in ruin and chaos, the Jin clan scattered; the multitude's feeling was righteous rising, the will to save those in mud and charcoal; yet you gentlemen thereupon saw me pushed and compelled, placed above kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin house collapsed and decent men rose to rescue the people from slaughter; you then thrust me, unwillingly, into a seat above kings and dukes.

sentences.zh: 本之基業，功由先帝。

translations.literal: The foundation of the base enterprise, merit comes from the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The foundation we stand on was laid by my late father’s merit.”

sentences.zh: 吾兄嫡統，丕祚所歸，恢懿明睿，殆天報命，大事垂克，薨于戎戰。

translations.literal: My elder brother's legitimate line, the great fortune returns to; vast, virtuous, bright, wise—perhaps Heaven's repayment of mandate; the great affair was about to be overcome; he died in military campaign.
translations.idiomatic: My elder brother embodied the legitimate line Heaven meant to bless—magnanimous, wise, clearly destined—yet he fell in battle just as victory was within reach.

sentences.zh: 班姿性仁孝，好學夙成，必為名器。

translations.literal: Ban's bearing and nature are humane and filial; he loves learning and early matured; he will surely become a vessel of renown.
translations.idiomatic: Ban is humane, filial, and precociously learned—he will grow into a true instrument of state.”

sentences.zh: 」李驤與司徒王達諫曰：「先王樹塚嫡者，所以防篡奪之萌，不可不慎。

translations.literal: " Li Xiang and Minister over the Masses Wang Da remonstrated saying, "The former kings established the tomb-heir—thereby to guard against the sprout of usurpation; one cannot but be careful.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang and Minister Wang Da objected: “Ancient kings invested the eldest legitimate son precisely to forestall usurpation; this is not a step to take lightly.”

sentences.zh: 吳子舍其子而立其弟，所以有專諸之禍；

translations.literal: The Wu ruler abandoned his son and established his younger brother—therefore there was the disaster of Zhuan Zhu;
translations.idiomatic: King Zhouliao of Wu passed over his son for a younger brother and brought down Zhuan Zhu’s dagger.

sentences.zh: 宋宣不立與夷而立穆公，卒有宋督之變。

translations.literal: Song Xuan did not establish Yu Yi but established Duke Mu; in the end there was the Song Du change.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xuan of Song preferred Duke Mu to his own heir and reaped the coup of Hua Du.

sentences.zh: 猶子之言，豈若子也？

translations.literal: A nephew's words—how can they compare to a son?
translations.idiomatic: How can a nephew ever stand comparison with a son?”

sentences.zh: 深願陛下思之。

translations.literal: We deeply hope Your Majesty will ponder it.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to weigh this with care.”

sentences.zh: 」雄不從，竟立班，驤退而流涕曰：「亂自此始矣！」

translations.literal: " Xiong did not follow; in the end he established Ban; Xiang withdrew and shed tears saying, "Disorder from this begins!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong ignored the advice, invested Li Ban anyway, whereupon Li Xiang withdrew in tears, declaring, “This is where the trouble starts.”

sentences.zh: 張駿遣使遺雄書，勸去尊號，稱籓于晉。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun sent an envoy leaving Xiong a letter, urging removal of the exalted title, declaring vassalage to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun sent a letter urging Li Xiong to drop his imperial title and acknowledge Jin as suzerain.

sentences.zh: 雄復書曰：「吾過為士大夫所推，然本無心於帝王也，進思為晉室元功之臣，退思共為守籓之將，掃除氛埃，以康帝宇。

translations.literal: Xiong replied in a letter saying, "I was excessively pushed by the gentry, yet originally I had no heart for emperor and king; advancing I thought to be a chief merit minister of the Jin house, retreating I thought together to be generals guarding the domain, sweeping away miasma, thereby to bring peace to the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong answered: “Gentlemen pressed me further than I wished; I never coveted the throne. At best I hoped to serve Jin as a founding minister; at least to hold the frontier beside other loyal generals and clear the air so the house of Sima might recover.”

sentences.zh: 而晉室陵遲，德聲不振，引領東望，有年月矣。

translations.literal: But the Jin house declined; virtuous fame did not rise; stretching neck eastward gazing—there have been years and months.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jin withered and its moral prestige failed; I have strained toward the east for years on end.”

sentences.zh: 會獲來貺，情在暗室，有何已已。

translations.literal: When I obtained what came as gift, feeling was in the dark chamber—what end is there.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving your gracious letter stirs the same private gratitude I would feel in secret—how could it ever be exhausted?”

sentences.zh: 知欲遠遵楚、漢，尊崇義帝，《春秋》之義，于斯莫大。

translations.literal: I know you wish distantly to follow Chu and Han, honoring and revering Emperor Yi; the meaning of the Spring and Autumn, in this there is nothing greater.
translations.idiomatic: I understand you mean to echo the Chu–Han settlement that honored Emperor Yi—no gesture could better match the spirit of the Spring and Autumn annals.”

sentences.zh: 」駿重其言，使聘相繼。

translations.literal: " Jun esteemed his words; envoys succeeded one another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun respected the tone and kept embassies moving between them.

sentences.zh: 巴郡嘗告急，雲有東軍。

translations.literal: Baxi once reported emergency, saying there were eastern armies.
translations.idiomatic: Ba commandery once sent word of an emergency—eastern troops were said to be advancing.

sentences.zh: 雄曰：「吾嘗慮石勒跋扈，侵逼琅邪，以為耿耿。

translations.literal: Xiong said, "I once worried Shi Le was overbearing, encroaching and pressing Langye—I took it as anxious.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong remarked, “I used to fret that Shi Le’s arrogance would swallow the Langye prince—that thought gnawed at me.”

sentences.zh: 不圖乃能舉兵，使人欣然。

translations.literal: I did not scheme that he could raise troops, making people joyful.
translations.idiomatic: I never expected him actually to take the field—news of it delights me.”

sentences.zh: 」雄之雅譚，多如此類。

translations.literal: " Xiong's refined conversations were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Li Xiong’s polished remarks ran in this vein.

sentences.zh: 雄以中原喪亂，乃頻遣使朝貢，與晉穆帝分天下。

translations.literal: Xiong because the Central Plain was in ruin and chaos, thereupon frequently sent envoys to offer court tribute, dividing the realm with Jin Emperor Mu.
translations.idiomatic: With the Central Plains in chaos, Li Xiong repeatedly sent tribute missions and tacitly partitioned influence with Emperor Mu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 張駿領秦、梁，先是，遣傅穎假道於蜀，通表京師，雄弗許。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun commanded Qin and Liang; before this, he sent Fu Ying to borrow passage through Shu to communicate memorials to the capital; Xiong did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, who held Qin and Liang, once asked Fu Ying to seek transit through Shu so he could forward memorials to the Jin court; Li Xiong refused.

sentences.zh: 駿又遣治中從事張淳稱籓於蜀，托以假道。

translations.literal: Jun again sent Administrative Aide Zhang Chun to declare vassalage to Shu, using as pretext borrowing passage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun next sent his administrative aide Zhang Chun to profess vassalage to Shu while asking safe passage through its territory.

sentences.zh: 雄大悅，謂淳曰：「貴主英名蓋世，土險兵強，何不自稱帝一方？

translations.literal: Xiong was greatly pleased and said to Chun, "Your noble lord's heroic name covers the age; the land is perilous and the troops strong—why not for yourself proclaim emperor over a region?
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Li Xiong said to Zhang Chun, “Your master’s fame towers over the age, his terrain is formidable and his soldiers strong—why not simply declare himself emperor in his own quarter?”

sentences.zh: 」淳曰：「寡君以乃祖世濟忠良，未能雪天下之恥，解眾人之倒懸，日昃忘食，枕戈待旦。

translations.literal: " Chun said, "Our poor lord, because your ancestors for generations aided loyalty and goodness, has been unable to wash away the realm's shame, release the multitude's inverted hanging; the sun declines forgetting food, pillowing spear awaiting dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun replied, “My lord’s house has for generations served Jin with loyalty; he burns to avenge the empire’s humiliation and lift the people from their peril—he skips meals as the sun sets and sleeps with his spear beside him, waiting for dawn.”

sentences.zh: 以琅邪中興江東，故萬里翼戴，將成桓文之事，何言自取邪！

translations.literal: Because Langye revives Jiangdong, therefore for ten thousand li they wing and uphold, about to accomplish the deeds of Huan and Wen—how speak of taking for oneself!
translations.idiomatic: The Langye prince is reviving the dynasty east of the Yangzi, so we rally to him from afar, hoping to repeat the achievements of Duke Huan and Duke Wen—how can you speak of seizing the throne for ourselves?”

sentences.zh: 」雄有慚色，曰：「我乃祖乃父亦是晉臣，往與六郡避難此地，為同盟所推，遂有今日。

translations.literal: " Xiong had a shameful color and said, "My grandfather and father too were Jin ministers; formerly with the six commanderies we fled disaster to this place, was pushed by the alliance partners, and thereupon have today.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong colored with embarrassment and said, “My forebears were also servants of Jin; we took refuge here from the six commanderies and were raised up by our allies—only that brought us to where we are.”

sentences.zh: 琅邪若能中興大晉於中夏，亦當率眾輔之。

translations.literal: If Langye can in the Central Xia revive great Jin, I too ought to lead the multitude to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: If the Langye prince can restore great Jin in the heartland, I will lead my hosts to support him.”

sentences.zh: 」淳還，通表京師，天子嘉之。

translations.literal: " Chun returned, communicated memorials to the capital, and the Son of Heaven praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun went home, forwarded the memorials to the Jin court, and the emperor commended the exchange.

sentences.zh: 時李驤死，以其子壽為大將軍、西夷校尉，督征南費黑、征東任回攻陷巴東，太守楊謙退保建平。

translations.literal: At the time Li Xiang died; he appointed his son Shou as Grand General, Colonel of the Western Yi, supervising South-conquering Fei Hei and East-conquering Ren Hui to attack and take Badong; the Administrator Yang Qian withdrew to hold Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiang died, his son Li Shou succeeded him as grand general and colonel of the western tribes, directing Fei Hei on the southern front and Ren Hui on the east; they seized Badong and forced Governor Yang Qian back into Jianping.

sentences.zh: 壽別遣費黑寇建平，晉巴東監軍毌丘奧退保宜都。

translations.literal: Shou separately sent Fei Hei to raid Jianping; Jin Badong Army Supervisor Guanqiu Ao withdrew to hold Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou also sent Fei Hei against Jianping, driving Jin’s Badong supervisor Guanqiu Ao to fall back on Yidu.

sentences.zh: 雄遣李壽攻硃提，以費黑、仰攀為前鋒，又遣鎮南任回征木落，分寧州之援。

translations.literal: Xiong sent Li Shou to attack Zhuti, with Fei Hei and Yang Pan as vanguard; again he sent South-garrisoning Ren Hui to campaign against Muluo, dividing Ning Province's relief.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong ordered Li Shou against Zhuti with Fei Hei and Yang Pan in the van, and sent Ren Hui south to strike Muluo, cutting off relief to Ning province.

sentences.zh: 甯州刺史尹奉降，遂有南中之地。

translations.literal: Inspector of Ning Province Yin Feng surrendered; thereupon he had the lands of southern center.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Yin Feng of Ning capitulated, and the southern basin fell under Li Xiong’s control.

sentences.zh: 雄於是赦其境內，使班討平寧州夷，以班為撫軍。

translations.literal: Xiong thereupon amnestied his territory, sent Ban to campaign and pacify the Ning Province Yi, and appointed Ban as Army-soothing.
translations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed a general amnesty, sent Li Ban to subdue the tribes of Ning province, and named him general of the pacification army.

sentences.zh: ，雄生瘍於頭，六日死，時年六十一，在位三十年。

translations.literal: , Xiong developed a sore on the head; in six days he died; at the time age sixty-one; on the throne thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong developed a festering sore on his head; six days later he was dead, aged sixty-one, having reigned thirty years.

sentences.zh: 偽諡武帝，廟曰太宗，墓號安都陵。

translations.literal: Falsely posthumous title Emperor Wu, temple called Taizong, tomb title Andu Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: His regime honored him posthumously as Emperor Wu, gave his temple the name Taizong, and called his tomb the Andu mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 雄性寬厚，簡刑約法，甚有名稱。

translations.literal: Xiong's nature was lenient and generous; he simplified punishments and restrained laws; he had very great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong was magnanimous by nature, pared penalties, and kept statutes lean, and his reputation for it was excellent.

sentences.zh: 氐苻成、隗文既降復叛，手傷雄母，及其來也，咸釋其罪，厚加待納。

translations.literal: The Di Fu Cheng and Wei Wen having surrendered again rebelled, by hand injured Xiong's mother; when they came, he all released their crimes and generously treated and received them.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftains Fu Cheng and Wei Wen had wounded Li Xiong’s mother when they rebelled after submitting; when they came back he forgave them outright and welcomed them with generous treatment.

sentences.zh: 由是夷夏安之，威震四土。

translations.literal: From this the Yi and Xia were settled; might shook the four lands.
translations.idiomatic: Tribesmen and Chinese alike settled down under his rule, and his prestige reached every quarter.

sentences.zh: 時海內大亂，而蜀獨無事，故歸之者相尋。

translations.literal: At the time within the seas was great chaos, but Shu alone had no troubles; therefore those who returned to him followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: While the empire convulsed, Shu alone stayed calm, so refugees flocked to him in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 雄乃興學校，置史官，聽覽之暇，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Xiong thereupon raised schools, established historiographers; in the leisure of listening and perusing, hand did not release scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He founded schools, appointed court historians, and in the intervals of government he was never without a book in hand.

sentences.zh: 其賦男丁歲穀三斛，女丁半之，戶調絹不過數丈，綿數兩。

translations.literal: His levy: male adults yearly grain three hu; female adults half it; household silk levy not exceeding several zhang of plain silk, several liang of floss.
translations.idiomatic: Male taxpayers owed three hu of grain a year, women half that; the household silk levy was only a few bolts and a few ounces of floss.

sentences.zh: 事少役稀，百姓富貴，閭門不閉，無相侵盜。

translations.literal: Affairs few, corvée sparse; the hundred surnames wealthy and noble; lane gates not closed; none mutually encroached or stole.
translations.idiomatic: With light government and rare labor service the people grew prosperous; doors were left unbarred and theft all but unknown.

sentences.zh: 然雄意在招致遠方，國用不足，故諸將每進金銀珍寶，多有以得官者。

translations.literal: Yet Xiong's intention was to summon the distant; state expenditure was insufficient; therefore the generals often presented gold, silver, and precious treasures; many there were who by this obtained office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he meant to draw in men from afar while revenue ran short, so generals often bought posts by presenting gold, silver, and curios.

sentences.zh: 丞相楊褒諫曰：「陛下為天下主，當網羅四海，何有以官買金邪！

translations.literal: Chancellor Yang Bao remonstrated saying, "Your Majesty is master of the realm; ought to net and gather the four seas—how can there be buying gold with office!
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yang Bao objected: “As sovereign you should cast the net wide across the realm—how can offices be traded for bullion?”

sentences.zh: 」雄遜辭謝之。

translations.literal: " Xiong with modest words thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong apologized meekly and took the rebuke to heart.

sentences.zh: 後雄嘗酒醉而推中書令，杖太官令，褒進曰：「天子穆穆，諸侯皇皇，安有天子而為酗也！

translations.literal: Later Xiong once when drunk pushed the Palace Secretary, caned the Grand Provisioner; Bao advanced saying, "The Son of Heaven is solemn; the feudal lords are august—how can there be a Son of Heaven who acts drunk!
translations.idiomatic: Once, drunk, Li Xiong shoved his palace secretary and beat the chief of provisions; Yang Bao stepped forward: “The Son of Heaven should be grave and lords awe-inspiring—what emperor behaves like a sot?”

sentences.zh: 」雄即舍之。

translations.literal: " Xiong immediately released them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong at once let the two officials go.

sentences.zh: 雄無事小出，褒於後持矛馳馬過雄。

translations.literal: Xiong on a minor outing without affair, Bao behind grasping spear galloped horse past Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: During a casual outing Li Xiong suddenly saw Yang Bao gallop past him from behind with a spear leveled.

sentences.zh: 雄怪問之，對曰：「夫統天下之重，如臣乘惡馬而持矛也，急之則慮自傷，緩之則懼其失，是以馬馳而不制也。

translations.literal: Xiong wondered and asked him; he replied saying, "The weight of uniting the realm is like your servant riding a bad horse while grasping a spear: press urgently then worry about self-injury; slacken then fear its loss; therefore the horse gallops and is not controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Startled, Li Xiong asked what this meant; Yang Bao answered, “Bearing the realm is like riding a vicious mount with a spear in hand: spur too hard and you wound yourself, slacken the reins and you lose control—hence the horse runs wild.”

sentences.zh: 」雄寤，即還。

translations.literal: " Xiong awoke, immediately returned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong took the point and turned back at once.

sentences.zh: 雄為國無威儀，官無祿秩，班序不別，君子小人服章不殊；

translations.literal: Xiong as for the state had no awe-inspiring demeanor; offices had no salary ranks; order of precedence was not distinguished; gentleman and petty man garment insignia not different;
translations.idiomatic: His court lacked ceremony; offices carried no fixed salaries or seniority; gentlemen and commoners dressed alike;

sentences.zh: 行軍無號令，用兵無部隊，戰勝不相讓，敗不相救，攻城破邑動以虜獲為先。

translations.literal: marching armies had no commands; using troops had no units; victory in battle did not yield to each other; defeat did not rescue each other; attacking cities and breaking towns moved with taking captives and booty as first.
translations.idiomatic: campaigns ran without clear orders or formed units; victors squabbled over spoils while defeated units were left to die; storming towns meant grabbing loot first and asking questions later.

sentences.zh: 此其所以失也。

translations.literal: This is the reason for his losing.
translations.idiomatic: These were the seeds of his house’s eventual fall.

sentences.zh: 李班

translations.literal: Li Ban
translations.idiomatic: Li Ban

sentences.zh: 班字世文。

translations.literal: Ban, courtesy name Shiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ban, courtesy name Shiwen.

sentences.zh: 初署平南將軍，後立為太子。

translations.literal: Initially he was titular South-pacifying General; afterward established as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He first held the title of general who pacifies the south, then was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 班謙虛博納，敬愛儒賢，自何點、李釗，班皆師之，又引名士王嘏及隴西董融、天水文夔等以為賓友。

translations.literal: Ban was modest and broadly receptive, respected and loved Confucian worthies; from He Dian, Li Zhao, Ban all took them as teachers; again he drew in eminent gentlemen Wang Gu and Longxi Dong Rong, Tianshui Wen Kui, and others as guest-friends.
translations.idiomatic: Humble and open-minded, he revered scholars, treating He Dian and Li Zhao as his teachers, and he gathered Wang Gu, Dong Rong of Longxi, Wen Kui of Tianshui, and other notables as companions.

sentences.zh: 每謂融等曰：「觀周景王太子晉、魏太子丕、吳太子孫登，文章鑒識，超然卓絕，未嘗不有慚色。

translations.literal: He often said to Rong and others, "Observing King Jing of Zhou's heir Prince Jin, Wei heir Prince Pi, Wu heir Sun Deng—their writings and critical insight, transcendent and outstanding—I never lack a shameful expression.
translations.idiomatic: He often told Dong Rong and the rest, “When I read of Prince Jin of Zhou, Cao Pi of Wei, and Sun Deng of Wu—men whose prose and judgment stood incomparably high—I cannot help feeling ashamed.”

sentences.zh: 何古賢之高朗，後人之莫逮也！

translations.literal: How the ancient worthies were high and bright; later men do not reach!
translations.idiomatic: How luminous those ancient paragons were, and how far we fall short today!”

sentences.zh: 」為性汎愛，動修軌度。

translations.literal: " His nature was broadly loving; in movement he cultivated norms and measure.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved widely and disciplined himself to observe proper bounds.

sentences.zh: 時諸李子弟皆尚奢靡，而班常戒厲之。

translations.literal: At the time the various Li sons and younger kin all esteemed luxury and extravagance, but Ban often warned and admonished them.
translations.idiomatic: While other members of the Li clan chased extravagance, Li Ban constantly chastened them.

sentences.zh: 每朝有大議，雄輒令豫之。

translations.literal: Whenever court had great deliberations, Xiong always ordered him to participate in them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever weighty policy was debated at court, Li Xiong insisted Li Ban take part.

sentences.zh: 班以古者墾田均平，貧富獲所，今貴者廣占荒田，貧者種殖無地，富者以己所餘而賣之，此豈王者大均之義乎！

translations.literal: Ban took that in antiquity reclaimed fields were equal and level, poor and rich each obtained their place; now the noble broadly occupy waste fields, the poor plant and have no land; the rich by what they themselves surplus sell it—how is this the kingly great leveling meaning!
translations.idiomatic: Li Ban argued that antiquity had balanced fields so rich and poor each had a place, whereas now magnates seized empty acres, peasants had nowhere to sow, and the wealthy peddled their surplus land—was that the equitable ideal of a true king?”

sentences.zh: 雄納之。

translations.literal: Xiong accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 及雄寢疾，班晝夜侍側。

translations.literal: When Xiong lay ill, Ban day and night attended at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiong fell mortally ill, Li Ban kept vigil day and night.

sentences.zh: 雄少數攻戰，多被傷夷，至是疾甚，痕皆膿潰，雄子越等惡而遠之。

translations.literal: Xiong in youth repeatedly in attacks and battles, many times received wounds; by now the illness was severe; scars all festered with pus; Xiong's sons Yue and others loathed and kept distant from him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong had been wounded often in his fighting days; now his scars festered, and sons such as Li Yue found the stench unbearable and shunned him.

sentences.zh: 班為吮膿，殊無難色，每嘗藥流涕，不脫衣冠，其孝誠如此。

translations.literal: Ban for him sucked pus, completely without difficult expression; whenever tasting medicine shed tears; did not remove cap and garments—his filial sincerity was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ban sucked the discharge without flinching, wept whenever he tasted Li Xiong’s medicine, and would not leave his side even to change—such was his devotion.

sentences.zh: 雄死，嗣偽位，以李壽錄尚書事輔政。

translations.literal: Xiong died; he succeeded to the false position; with Li Shou recording Masters of Writing affairs assisting government.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiong died, Li Ban succeeded him and put Li Shou in charge of the secretariat as regent.

sentences.zh: 班居中執喪禮，政事皆委壽及司徒何點、尚書令王瑰等。

translations.literal: Ban in the center observed mourning rites; government affairs all were entrusted to Shou and Minister over the Masses He Dian, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Wang Gui, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ban remained at court to observe mourning while Li Shou, Minister He Dian, Director Wang Gui, and others ran the government.

sentences.zh: 越時鎮江陽，以班非雄所生，意甚不平。

translations.literal: Yue at the time garrisoned Jiangyang; because Ban was not born of Xiong, his mind was very unbalanced.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yue, stationed at Jiangyang, deeply resented that Li Ban was not Li Xiong’s own son.

sentences.zh: 至此，奔喪，與其弟期密計圖之。

translations.literal: Coming to this, he rushed mourning, with his younger brother Qi secretly plotted to scheme against him.
translations.idiomatic: He came to the funeral and plotted secretly with his brother Li Qi to remove Li Ban.

sentences.zh: 李玝勸班遣越還江陽，以期為梁州刺史，鎮葭萌。

translations.literal: Li Yu urged Ban to send Yue back to Jiangyang, and appoint Qi as Inspector of Liang Province, garrisoning Jiameng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu urged Li Ban to send Li Yue back to Jiangyang and appoint Li Qi inspector of Liang province at Jiameng.

sentences.zh: 班以未葬，不忍遣，推誠居厚，心無纖芥。

translations.literal: Ban because not yet buried, could not bear to send; pushing sincerity dwelt in generosity; heart had no fiber or mustard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ban could not bring himself to banish them before the burial; he trusted them openly and harbored not the slightest suspicion.

sentences.zh: 時有白氣二道帶天，太史令韓豹奏：「宮中有陰謀兵氣，戒在親戚。

translations.literal: At the time there were two white vapors belts across heaven; Grand Astrologer Han Bao memorialized, "Within the palace there is secret-plot military qi; warning lies in kin.
translations.idiomatic: Two bands of white vapor spanned the sky; the grand astrologer Han Bao reported, “The palace shows the aura of intrigue and arms—the danger lies among your kinsmen.”

sentences.zh: 」班不悟。

translations.literal: " Ban did not awaken.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ban paid no heed.

sentences.zh: ，班因夜哭，越殺班于殯宮，時年四十七，在位一年，遂立雄之子期嗣位焉。

translations.literal: , Ban because night weeping, Yue killed Ban in the funerary palace; at the time age forty-seven; on the throne one year; thereupon established Xiong's son Qi to succeed the position.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Ban kept night vigil in mourning, Li Yue murdered him in the funerary hall; he was forty-seven and had reigned only a year before Li Qi, another son of Li Xiong, was enthroned.

sentences.zh: 李期

translations.literal: Li Qi
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi

sentences.zh: 期字世運，雄第四子也。

translations.literal: Qi, courtesy name Shiyun, was Xiong's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi, courtesy name Shiyun, was the fourth son of Li Xiong.

sentences.zh: 聰慧好學，弱冠能屬文，輕財好施，虛心招納。

translations.literal: Clever and fond of learning, at capping age able to compose texts; light on wealth fond of giving; empty mind summoning and receiving.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and bookish, he could write polished essays before twenty, spent money freely, and welcomed talent with genuine openness.

sentences.zh: 初為建威將軍，雄令諸子及宗室子弟以恩信合眾，多者不至數百，而期獨致千餘人。

translations.literal: Initially he was General Who Establishes Might; Xiong ordered the various sons and imperial clan sons and younger kin by grace and trust to gather multitudes; the many did not reach several hundred, but Qi alone brought more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His first post was general who establishes might; Li Xiong had each prince and kinsman raise followers on personal credit, and while others mustered only a few hundred, Li Qi enrolled well over a thousand.

sentences.zh: 其所表薦，雄多納之，故長史列署頗出其門。

translations.literal: What he memorial-recommended, Xiong mostly accepted; therefore chief clerks and ranked offices largely came out of his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong usually approved his nominations, so many senior clerks and bureau heads owed their posts to Li Qi’s patronage.

sentences.zh: 既殺班，欲立越為主，越以期雄妻任氏所養，又多才藝，乃讓位於期。

translations.literal: Having killed Ban, they wished to establish Yue as lord; Yue because Qi was raised by Xiong's wife the Lady Ren, and also had many talents and arts, thereupon yielded position to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After murdering Li Ban they meant to enthrone Li Yue, but Yue ceded the throne to Li Qi because Qi had been reared by Li Xiong’s empress Lady Ren and was the more capable man.

sentences.zh: 於是僭即皇帝位，大赦境內，改元玉恆。

translations.literal: Thereupon he usurpingly ascended the emperor position, greatly amnestied within the territory, changed era to Yuheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized the imperial title, ordered a general amnesty, and proclaimed the reign Yuheng.

sentences.zh: 誅班弟都。

translations.literal: He executed Ban's younger brother Du.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Li Ban’s brother Li Du.

sentences.zh: 使李壽伐都弟玝于涪，玝棄城降晉。

translations.literal: He sent Li Shou to campaign against Du's younger brother Yu at Fu; Yu abandoned the city and surrendered to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Shou against Li Yu at Fu; Li Yu abandoned the city and defected to Jin.

sentences.zh: 封壽漢王，拜梁州刺史、東羌校尉、中護軍、錄尚書事；

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Shou as King of Han, appointed Inspector of Liang Province, Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, Central Guards General, recording Masters of Writing affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou was enfeoffed as prince of Han and given the posts of inspector of Liang, colonel of the eastern Qiang, central protector-general, and director of the secretariat;

sentences.zh: 封兄越建甯王，拜相國、大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed elder brother Yue as King of Jianning, appointed Chancellor of State, Grand General, recording Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yue became prince of Jianning, chancellor of state, grand general, and co-director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 立妻閻氏為皇后。

translations.literal: He established his wife the Lady Yan as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He elevated his wife Lady Yan to empress.

sentences.zh: 以其衛將軍尹奉為右丞相、驃騎將軍、尚書令，王瑰為司徒。

translations.literal: He appointed his Guards General Yin Feng as Right Chancellor, Cavalry-on-the-Wing General, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; Wang Gui as Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Guard general Yin Feng was made right chancellor, chief cavalry commander, and director of the secretariat, while Wang Gui became minister over the masses.

sentences.zh: 期自以謀大事既果，輕諸舊臣，外則信任尚書令景騫、尚書姚華、田褒。

translations.literal: Qi himself because the great plot had succeeded, slighted the various old ministers; outwardly he trusted Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Jing Qian, Masters of Writing Yao Hua, Tian Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Confident after his coup, Li Qi scorned the elder statesmen and left policy to Director Jing Qian and the ministers Yao Hua and Tian Bao.

sentences.zh: 褒無他才藝，雄時勸立期，故寵待甚厚。

translations.literal: Bao had no other talents or arts; at the time of Xiong he urged establishing Qi; therefore favor and treatment were very thick.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Bao had little ability but had urged Li Xiong to favor Li Qi, so he now enjoyed extravagant patronage.

sentences.zh: 內則信宦豎許涪等。

translations.literal: Inwardly he trusted eunuchs Xu Fu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace he relied on eunuchs such as Xu Fu.

sentences.zh: 國之刑政，希復關之卿相，慶賞威刑，皆決數人而已，於是綱維紊矣。

translations.literal: The state's punishments and government, rarely again concerned the ministers and chancellors; rewards and honors, awe and punishments, all were decided by several men only; from this the guiding net was disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Justice and administration seldom reached the chief ministers; rewards, honors, and punishments were settled by a handful of favorites, and the machinery of state unraveled.

sentences.zh: 乃誣其尚書僕射、武陵公李載謀反，下獄死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he falsely accused his Deputy Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Wuling Li Zai of plotting rebellion; cast into prison he died.
translations.idiomatic: He framed Vice Director Li Zai, duke of Wuling, for treason and had him die in prison.

sentences.zh: 先是，晉建威將軍司馬勳屯漢中，期遣李壽攻而陷之，遂置守宰，戍南鄭。

translations.literal: Before this, Jin General Who Establishes Might Sima Xun garrisoned Hanzhong; Qi sent Li Shou to attack and take it; thereupon he placed guards and administrators, garrisoning Nan Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jin’s general Sima Xun had held Hanzhong until Li Qi sent Li Shou to conquer it; Li Qi then stationed officials and troops at Nan Zheng.

sentences.zh: 雄子霸、保並不病而死，皆云期鴆殺之，於是大臣懷懼，人不自安。

translations.literal: Xiong's sons Ba and Bao both without illness died; all said Qi poison-killed them; from this great ministers harbored fear; people were not self-at-ease.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong’s sons Li Ba and Li Bao died suddenly, and rumor blamed Li Qi’s poison; ministers grew fearful and no one felt safe.

sentences.zh: 天雨大魚于宮中，其色黃。

translations.literal: Heaven rained great fish in the palace; their color was yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Great yellow fish rained into the palace courtyards.

sentences.zh: 又宮中豕犬交。

translations.literal: Again in the palace pigs and dogs copulated.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palace swine and dogs were seen coupling.

sentences.zh: 期多所誅夷，籍沒婦女資財以實後庭，內外凶凶，道路以目，諫者獲罪，人懷苟免。

translations.literal: Qi many executed and extirpated; registered and confiscated women and property to fill the rear court; inner and outer violent-violent; on roads with eyes; remonstrators got crime; people harbored careless escape.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi slaughtered widely, seized women and wealth to stock his harem, and spread terror inside and out until people exchanged only glances on the road; advisers who spoke up were punished, and everyone sought merely to survive.

sentences.zh: 期又鴆殺其安北李攸。

translations.literal: Qi again poison-killed his Defender of the North Li You.
translations.idiomatic: He also poisoned his defender of the north, Li You.

sentences.zh: 攸，壽之養弟也。

translations.literal: You was Shou's foster younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Li You was a foster brother of Li Shou.

sentences.zh: 於是與越及景騫、田褒、姚華謀襲壽等，欲因燒市橋而發兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Yue and Jing Qian, Tian Bao, Yao Hua they plotted to raid Shou and others, wishing by burning the market bridge to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi then conspired with Li Yue, Jing Qian, Tian Bao, and Yao Hua to strike Li Shou, planning to torch the market bridge as the signal for troops.

sentences.zh: 期又累遣中常侍許涪至壽所，伺其動靜。

translations.literal: Qi again repeatedly sent Palace Attendant Xu Fu to Shou's place, to spy his movements.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi repeatedly sent the eunuch Xu Fu to Li Shou’s camp to watch his every move.

sentences.zh: 及殺攸，壽大懼，又疑許涪往來之數也，乃率步騎一萬，自涪向成都，表稱景騫、田褒亂政，興晉陽之甲，以除君側之惡。

translations.literal: When You was killed, Shou greatly feared; again he suspected Xu Fu's comings and goings were many; thereupon he led foot and horse ten thousand, from Fu toward Chengdu, memorial declaring Jing Qian and Tian Bao disordered government, raising Jin-yang armor, to remove evil beside the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: After Li You’s murder Li Shou panicked, suspecting Xu Fu’s constant visits heralded his own doom; he marched ten thousand infantry and cavalry from Fu toward Chengdu, memorializing that Jing Qian and Tian Bao had corrupted the government and that he was “raising the hosts of Jinyang” to purge evildoers from the ruler’s side.

sentences.zh: 以李奕為先登。

translations.literal: He appointed Li Yi as vanguard assaulter.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi led the assault column.

sentences.zh: 壽到成都，期、越不虞其至，素不備設，壽遂取其城，屯兵至門。

translations.literal: When Shou reached Chengdu, Qi and Yue did not expect his arrival; ordinarily had not prepared defenses; Shou thereupon took its city, encamped troops to the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou reached Chengdu before Li Qi and Li Yue expected; with no defenses ready he walked into the capital and drew up his men at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 期遣侍中勞壽，壽奏相國、建甯王越，尚書令、河南公景騫，尚書田褒、姚華，中常侍許涪，征西將軍李遐及將軍李西等，皆懷奸亂政，謀傾社稷，大逆不道，罪合夷滅。

translations.literal: Qi sent Palace Attendant to console Shou; Shou memorialized Chancellor of State, King of Jianning Yue, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Duke of Henan Jing Qian, Masters of Writing Tian Bao, Yao Hua, Palace Attendant Xu Fu, West-conquering General Li Xia and General Li Xi and others, all harbored treachery disordered government, plotted to overturn the altars of soil and grain, great rebellion not the Way, crime fitting extermination.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi sent an attendant to greet him; Li Shou submitted a bill of indictment naming Chancellor Li Yue, Director Jing Qian duke of Henan, ministers Tian Bao and Yao Hua, eunuch Xu Fu, generals Li Xia and Li Xi, and others as traitors who had ruined the state and deserved extirpation.

sentences.zh: 期從之，於是殺越、騫等。

translations.literal: Qi followed it; thereupon killed Yue, Qian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi acquiesced, and Li Yue, Jing Qian, and their faction were put to death.

sentences.zh: 壽矯任氏令，廢期為邛都縣公，幽之別宮。

translations.literal: Shou forged the Lady Ren's order, deposed Qi as Duke of Qiongdu County, imprisoned him in a separate palace.
translations.idiomatic: Forging an edict from Empress Dowager Ren, Li Shou demoted Li Qi to duke of Qiongdu county and locked him in a detached palace.

sentences.zh: 期歎曰：「天下主乃當為小縣公，不如死也！

translations.literal: Qi sighed saying, "A lord of the realm is now to be a small county duke—not equal to death!
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi sighed, “To fall from master of the realm to petty county noble—better to die!”

sentences.zh: 」，自縊而死，時年二十五，在位三年。

translations.literal: " He strangled himself and died; at the time age twenty-five; on the throne three years.
translations.idiomatic: He hanged himself at twenty-five, having reigned three years.

sentences.zh: 諡曰幽公。

translations.literal: Posthumous title said Duke You.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous title Duke You (“the Secluded”).

sentences.zh: 及葬，賜鸞輅九旒，余如王禮。

translations.literal: When buried, he was granted phoenix chariot nine liu; the rest like king rites.
translations.idiomatic: At burial he was granted an imperial hearse with nine pennants; the remaining observances matched those for a king.

sentences.zh: 雄之子皆為壽所殺。

translations.literal: Xiong's sons all were killed by Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou slaughtered every surviving son of Li Xiong.

sentences.zh: 李壽

translations.literal: Li Shou
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou

sentences.zh: 壽字武考，驤之子也。

translations.literal: Shou, courtesy name Wukao, was Xiang's son.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou, courtesy name Wukao, was the son of Li Xiang.

sentences.zh: 敏而好學，雅量豁然，少尚禮容，異于李氏諸子。

translations.literal: Keen and fond of learning, magnanimous capacity open and clear; in youth esteemed ritual deportment, different from the various sons of the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and studious, broad-minded and even-tempered, he cultivated ritual bearing as a youth and stood apart from the other Li princes.

sentences.zh: 雄奇其才，以為足荷重任，拜前將軍、督巴西軍事，遷征東將軍。

translations.literal: Xiong marveled at his talent, thought him sufficient to bear heavy responsibility, appointed Forward General, supervisor of Baxi military affairs, promoted to General Who Conquers the East.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong prized his ability, judged him fit for heavy duty, named him forward general and supervisor of military affairs in Baxi, then promoted him to general who conquers the east.

sentences.zh: 時年十九，聘處士譙秀以為賓客，盡其讜言，在巴西威惠甚著。

translations.literal: At the time age nineteen, he engaged reclus Qiao Xiu as guest-retainer, exhausted his forthright words; in Baxi might and kindness were very manifest.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he retained the recluse Qiao Xiu as adviser, heeded blunt counsel, and built a reputation in Baxi for both firm rule and generosity.

sentences.zh: 驤死，遷大將軍、大都督、侍中，封扶風公，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When Xiang died, he was promoted Grand General, Grand Commander-in-Chief, Palace Attendant, enfeoffed Duke of Fufeng, recording Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xiang’s death he rose to grand general, grand commander, palace attendant, duke of Fufeng, and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 征寧州，攻圍百餘日，悉平諸郡，雄大悅，封建甯王。

translations.literal: He campaigned against Ning Province; attacked and besieged more than a hundred days; entirely pacified the various commanderies; Xiong was greatly pleased, enfeoffed him King of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: His hundred-day siege of Ning province brought every commandery to heel; Li Xiong was delighted and created him prince of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 雄死，受遺輔政。

translations.literal: When Xiong died, he received testament to assist government.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiong died, Li Shou was named to the regency council by his final testament.

sentences.zh: 期立，改封漢王，食梁州五郡，領梁州刺史。

translations.literal: When Qi was established, his fief was changed to King of Han, eating five commanderies of Liang Province, concurrently Inspector of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Qi took the throne, Li Shou was re-enfeoffed as prince of Han with revenue from five Liang commanderies and the title of inspector of Liang.

sentences.zh: 壽威名遠振，深為李越、景騫等所憚，壽深憂之。

translations.literal: Shou's awesome name shook far; deeply by Li Yue, Jing Qian, and others was he feared; Shou deeply worried about it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou’s prestige alarmed Li Yue, Jing Qian, and their faction, and he lived in dread of them.

sentences.zh: 代李玝屯涪，每應期朝覲，常自陳邊疆寇警，不可曠鎮，故得不朝。

translations.literal: He replaced Li Yu garrisoning Fu; whenever responding to Qi's court audience, he always himself declared border alarms of raiders, could not leave the garrison vacant; therefore obtained not attending court.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Li Yu at Fu and, whenever summoned to Chengdu, pleaded frontier emergencies that required his presence—so he avoided court altogether.

sentences.zh: 壽又見期、越兄弟十餘人年方壯大，而並有強兵，懼不自全，乃數聘禮巴西龔壯。

translations.literal: Shou again saw Qi, Yue brothers more than ten persons' years just strong and great, and together had strong troops; fearing not self-preserving, thereupon repeatedly with hiring rites Baxi Gong Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi and Li Yue commanded more than ten adult brothers, each with seasoned troops; fearing for his life, Li Shou repeatedly tried to retain Gong Zhuang of Baxi with lavish offers.

sentences.zh: 壯雖不應聘，數往見壽。

translations.literal: Zhuang although did not accept hire, repeatedly went to see Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhuang declined office but visited Li Shou often.

sentences.zh: 時岷山崩，江水竭，壽惡之，每問壯以自安之術。

translations.literal: At the time Mount Min collapsed, Yangtze water dried; Shou loathed it, often asked Zhuang for arts of self-security.
translations.idiomatic: When Mount Min collapsed and the river ran dry, Li Shou took it as an ill omen and constantly asked Gong Zhuang how to protect himself.

sentences.zh: 壯以特殺其父及叔，欲假手報仇，未有其由，因說壽曰：「節下若能舍小從大，以危易安，則開國裂土，長為諸侯，名高桓文，勳流百代矣。

translations.literal: Zhuang because Te killed his father and uncle, wished to borrow hands to avenge, yet had no means; thereupon urged Shou saying, "If beneath your command you can abandon small and follow great, exchange peril for safety, then open state and split soil, long be a feudal lord, name high as Huan and Wen, merit flowing hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhuang still hated Li Te for murdering his father and uncle and hoped to use Li Shou as his instrument; he therefore urged him: “If you can set aside private risk for the larger design, you may carve out a realm, hold a feudal title forever, and win fame to rival the hegemons Huan and Wen, with glory for generations.”

sentences.zh: 」壽從之，陰與長史略陽羅恆、巴西解思明共謀據成都，稱籓歸順。

translations.literal: " Shou followed it; secretly with Chief Clerk Lüeyang Luo Heng, Baxi Xie Siming together plotted to occupy Chengdu, declare vassalage and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou agreed and secretly plotted with his chief clerk Luo Heng of Lüeyang and Xie Siming of Baxi to seize Chengdu and offer allegiance to Jin.

sentences.zh: 乃誓文武，得數千人，襲成都，克之，縱兵虜掠，至乃奸略雄女及李氏諸婦，多所殘害，數日乃定。

translations.literal: Thereupon he swore civil and military, obtained several thousand men, raided Chengdu, overcame it, released troops to capture and plunder, reaching to raping and seizing Xiong's daughters and Li clan various women, many were harmed and killed; several days then settled.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied several thousand civil and military followers, stormed Chengdu, and took it; his troops ran wild, raping Li Xiong’s daughters and other Li women until the slaughter subsided only after days of chaos.

sentences.zh: 恆與思明及李奕、王利等勸壽稱鎮西將軍、益州牧、成都王，稱籓于晉，而任調與司馬蔡興、侍中李豔及張烈等勸壽自立。

translations.literal: Heng and Siming and Li Yi, Wang Li and others urged Shou to style himself General Who Guards the West, Governor of Yi, King of Chengdu, declare vassalage to Jin; but Ren Tiao with Cai Xing, Palace Attendant Li Yan, and Zhang Lie and others urged Shou to establish himself.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Heng, Xie Siming, Li Yi, and Wang Li wanted Li Shou to take the titles of general guarding the west, shepherd of Yi, and king of Chengdu under Jin, while Ren Tiao, Cai Xing, Li Yan, Zhang Lie, and others pressed him to declare his own dynasty.

sentences.zh: 壽命筮之，占者曰：「可數年天子。

translations.literal: Shou ordered divining it; the diviner said, "Can be several years Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou had the matter divined; the oracle reader said, “You may reign as Son of Heaven for a few years.”

sentences.zh: 」調喜曰：「一日尚為足，而況數年乎！

translations.literal: " Tiao rejoiced saying, "One day still is enough—how much more several years!
translations.idiomatic: Ren Tiao exclaimed, “A single day on the throne would satisfy me—let alone several years!”

sentences.zh: 」思明曰：「數年天子，孰與百世諸侯！

translations.literal: " Siming said, "Several years Son of Heaven—how does it compare to hundred generations feudal lord!
translations.idiomatic: Xie Siming retorted, “A few years as emperor—how does that weigh against generations as a loyal prince?”

sentences.zh: 」壽曰：「朝聞道，夕死可矣。

translations.literal: " Shou said, "Morning hear the Way, evening die may.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou answered, “If I grasp the Way at dawn, I may die at dusk content.”

sentences.zh: 任侯之言，策之上也。

translations.literal: Ren Tiao's words are the top of strategies.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Tiao’s counsel is the superior strategy.”

sentences.zh: 」遂以咸康四年僭即偽位，赦其境內，改元為漢興。

translations.literal: " Thereupon in the fourth year of Xiankang he usurpingly ascended the false position, amnestied his territory, changed era to Hanxing.
translations.idiomatic: In 338 he seized the throne, proclaimed an amnesty, and adopted the reign name Hanxing.

sentences.zh: 以董皎為相國，羅恆、馬當為股肱，李奕、任調、李閎為爪牙，解思明為謀主。

translations.literal: He appointed Dong Jiao as Chancellor of State, Luo Heng and Ma Dang as thigh and arm, Li Yi, Ren Tiao, Li Hong as claws and fangs, Xie Siming as plot master.
translations.idiomatic: He named Dong Jiao chancellor, made Luo Heng and Ma Dang his chief pillars, Li Yi, Ren Tiao, and Li Hong his enforcers, and Xie Siming his principal strategist.

sentences.zh: 以安車束帛聘龔壯為太師，壯固辭，特聽縞巾素帶，居師友之位。

translations.literal: With peace chariot and bundled silks he engaged Gong Zhuang as Grand Preceptor; Zhuang firmly declined; specially permitted white headcloth and plain belt, dwelling in teacher-friend position.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a carriage and silk to appoint Gong Zhuang grand preceptor; Gong Zhuang refused, so Li Shou allowed him to wear plain scholar’s dress and hold the honorary rank of mentor.

sentences.zh: 拔擢幽滯，處之顯列。

translations.literal: He raised the hidden and stuck, placed them in illustrious ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted overlooked talent to high office.

sentences.zh: 追尊父驤為獻帝，母昝氏為太后，立妻閻氏為皇后，世子勢為太子。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored father Xiang as Emperor Xian, mother the Lady Zan as empress dowager, established wife the Lady Yan as empress, heir-apparent Shi as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He canonized Li Xiang as Emperor Xian, elevated Lady Zan to empress dowager, named Lady Yan empress, and invested Li Shi as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 有告廣漢太守李乾與大臣通謀，欲廢壽者。

translations.literal: Someone reported Administrator of Guanghan Li Qian conspired with great ministers, wishing to depose Shou.
translations.idiomatic: An informant accused Governor Li Qian of Guanghan of plotting with senior officials to depose Li Shou.

sentences.zh: 壽令其子廣與大臣盟于前殿，徙乾漢嘉太守。

translations.literal: Shou ordered his son Guang with great ministers to covenant in the front hall, moved Qian to Administrator of Hanjia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou made his son Li Guang swear a pact with the ministers in the front hall and transferred Li Qian to the Hanjia governorship.

sentences.zh: 大風暴雨，震其端門。

translations.literal: Great wind and violent rain; shook his main gate.
translations.idiomatic: A violent storm struck and lightning hit the main palace gate.

sentences.zh: 壽深自悔責，命群臣極盡忠言，勿拘忌諱。

translations.literal: Shou deeply blamed himself, ordered the host of ministers exhaust loyal words, do not be bound by taboos.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply shaken, Li Shou blamed himself and ordered his officials to speak bluntly without fear of taboo.

sentences.zh: 遣其散騎常侍王嘏、中常侍王廣聘于石季龍。

translations.literal: He sent his Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Wang Gu, Palace Attendant Wang Guang to court Shi Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Wang Gu as cavalier attendant and the eunuch Wang Guang on an embassy to Shi Hu (Shi Jilong).

sentences.zh: 先是，季龍遺壽書，欲連橫入寇，約分天下。

translations.literal: Before this, Jilong left Shou a letter, wishing to join horizontal alliance to invade, covenant to divide the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shi Hu had written proposing a joint strike against Jin and a partition of the empire.

sentences.zh: 壽大悅，乃大修船艦，嚴兵繕甲，吏卒皆備候糧。

translations.literal: Shou was greatly pleased; thereupon greatly repaired ships and vessels, strict troops repaired armor; clerks and soldiers all prepared provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Li Shou launched a crash program—building warships, drilling troops, repairing armor, and stockpiling grain for every unit.

sentences.zh: 以其尚書令馬當為六軍都督，假節鉞，營東場大閱，軍士七萬餘人，舟師溯江而上。

translations.literal: He appointed his Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Ma Dang as commander of six armies, granted credentials and axe; encamped east field great review; soldiers more than seventy thousand; naval forces went upriver.
translations.idiomatic: Director Ma Dang became commander of the six armies with imperial baton and axe; Li Shou reviewed more than seventy thousand men at the eastern parade ground and sent the fleet up the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 過成都，鼓噪盈江，壽登城觀之。

translations.literal: Passing Chengdu, drum-noise filled the river; Shou ascended the wall to observe it.
translations.idiomatic: As the flotilla passed Chengdu, cheers shook the riverbanks; Li Shou mounted the wall to watch.

sentences.zh: 其群臣咸曰：「我國小眾寡，吳、會險遠，圖之未易。

translations.literal: His host of ministers all said, "Our state is small, multitude few; Wu and Kuai are perilous and far; to scheme them is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers protested: “We are a small state with few people; Wu and the southeast are remote and defensible—not an easy prize.”

sentences.zh: 」解思明又切諫懇至，壽於是命群臣陳其利害。

translations.literal: " Xie Siming again earnestly remonstrated sincerely; Shou thereupon ordered the host of ministers to state its benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Siming pleaded urgently, so Li Shou told the court to debate the merits and risks openly.

sentences.zh: 龔壯諫曰：「陛下與胡通，孰如與晉通？

translations.literal: Gong Zhuang remonstrated saying, "Your Majesty with the Hu communicating—how does it compare to with Jin communicating?
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhuang objected: “Is an alliance with the Hu tribes wiser than friendship with Jin?”

sentences.zh: 胡，豺狼國也。

translations.literal: The Hu is a jackal-wolf state.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu realm is a pack of wolves.”

sentences.zh: 晉既滅，不得不北面事之。

translations.literal: When Jin is destroyed, inevitably must face north and serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jin falls you will have no choice but to bow northward as their vassal.

sentences.zh: 若與之爭天下，則強弱勢異。

translations.literal: If with them contend for the realm, then strong-weak situation differs.
translations.idiomatic: Pitting ourselves against them for the empire reverses the balance of strength.”

sentences.zh: 此虞、虢之成范，已然之明戒，願陛下熟慮之。

translations.literal: This is Yu and Guo's completed model, already-so bright warning; hope Your Majesty carefully considers it.
translations.idiomatic: The fate of Yu and Guo is proof enough; I beg you to weigh it carefully.”

sentences.zh: 」群臣以壯之言為然，叩頭泣諫，壽乃止，士眾咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: " The host of ministers took Zhuang's words as right, knocked heads weeping remonstration; Shou thereupon stopped; soldiers all shouted ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The court endorsed Gong Zhuang’s argument and wept as they kowtowed; Li Shou canceled the expedition, and the troops cheered.

sentences.zh: 遣其鎮東大將軍李奕征牂柯，太守謝恕保城距守者積日，不拔。
