translations.literal: He sent his East-garrisoning Grand General Li Yi to campaign against Zangke; the Administrator Xie Shu held the city resisting for accumulated days; not taken.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Yi, his grand general guarding the east, against Zangke, but Governor Xie Shu held the walls for many days without yielding.

sentences.zh: 會奕糧盡，引還。

translations.literal: When Yi's grain was exhausted, he led back.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi withdrew when his supplies ran out.

sentences.zh: 壽以其太子勢領大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Shou appointed his heir-apparent Shi concurrently Grand General, recording Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou added to Crown Prince Li Shi the titles of grand general and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 壽承雄寬儉，新行篡奪，因循雄政，未逞其志欲。

translations.literal: Shou inherited Xiong's lenience and frugality; newly having carried out usurpation, he followed along Xiong's government, not yet indulging his will and desires.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou had inherited Li Xiong’s lenient, frugal rule; fresh from his coup, he still followed the old policies and had not yet indulged his own appetites.

sentences.zh: 會李閎、王嘏從鄴還，盛稱季龍威強，宮觀美麗，鄴中殷實。

translations.literal: When Li Hong, Wang Gu returned from Ye, they greatly praised Jilong's awesome strength, palace observatories beautiful, Ye center abundant and solid.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hong and Wang Gu returned from Ye they rhapsodized over Shi Hu’s might, the splendor of his palaces, and the wealth of his capital.

sentences.zh: 壽又聞季龍虐用刑法，王遜亦以殺罰禦下，並能控制邦域，壽心欣慕，人有小過，輒殺以立威。

translations.literal: Shou again heard Jilong cruelly used punishments and law; Wang Xun also by killing and penalties controlled subordinates; both were able to control the state domain; Shou's heart admired; people had small faults, then killed to establish awe.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou learned that Shi Hu ruled through terror and that Wang Xun had cowed his province with executions—both kept their domains in line. Envying them, Li Shou began executing men for petty faults to instill fear.

sentences.zh: 又以郊甸未實，都邑空虛，工匠器械，事未充盈，乃徙旁郡戶三丁已上以實成都，興尚方禦府，發州郡工巧以充之，廣修宮室，引水入城，務於奢侈。

translations.literal: Again because suburbs and outskirts were not full, capital and cities empty and void, artisans and tools, affairs not abundant and full, thereupon moved neighboring commandery households three adult males and above to fill Chengdu, raised Imperial Workshop and imperial treasury, issued commandery craftsmen to fill them, broadly built palaces and chambers, led water into the city, striving in extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: The capital region lay half empty and workshops understocked, so he relocated every household with three adult males from neighboring commanderies into Chengdu, expanded the imperial workshops, conscripted skilled labor from the provinces, threw up palaces on a grand scale, and brought river water into the city in pursuit of ostentation.

sentences.zh: 又廣太學，起宴殿。

translations.literal: Again he broadened the Imperial Academy, raised banquet halls.
translations.idiomatic: He enlarged the imperial academy and built banquet halls.

sentences.zh: 百姓疲于使役，呼嗟滿道，思亂者十室而九矣。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames tired in corvée service; sighs filled the roads; those thinking rebellion—nine of ten houses.
translations.idiomatic: The people groaned under labor levies; laments filled every road, and nine houses in ten were ready to rise.

sentences.zh: 其左僕射蔡興切諫，壽以為誹謗，誅之。

translations.literal: His Left Deputy Supervisor Cai Xing earnestly remonstrated; Shou took it as slander, executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Left vice director Cai Xing remonstrated bluntly; Li Shou called it slander and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 右僕射李嶷數以直言懺旨，壽積忿非一，托以他罪，下獄殺之。

translations.literal: Right Deputy Supervisor Li Yi repeatedly by straight words offended intent; Shou accumulated resentments not one; on pretext of other crimes, cast into prison and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Right vice director Li Yi often spoke plainly and offended Li Shou, who nursed many grudges, framed him on other charges, and executed him in prison.

sentences.zh: 壽疾篤，常見李期、蔡興為祟。

translations.literal: Shou's illness was severe; he constantly saw Li Qi, Cai Xing as haunting spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In his final illness Li Shou was haunted by visions of Li Qi and Cai Xing.

sentences.zh: 八年，壽死，時年四十四，在位五年。

translations.literal: The eighth year, Shou died; at the time age forty-four; on the throne five years.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Hanxing he died at forty-four, having reigned five years.

sentences.zh: 偽諡昭文帝，廟曰中宗，墓曰安昌陵。

translations.literal: False posthumous title Emperor Zhaowen, temple called Zhongzong, tomb called Anchang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: His state gave him the posthumous title Emperor Zhaowen, the temple name Zhongzong, and buried him at the Anchang mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 壽初為王，好學愛士，庶幾善道，每覽良將賢相建功立事者，未嘗不反覆誦之，故能征伐四克，辟國千里。

translations.literal: When Shou first was king, he loved learning and cherished gentlemen, nearly good Way; whenever perusing good generals and worthy chancellors who established merit and accomplished affairs, never did he not repeatedly recite them; therefore able in campaigns and attacks fourfold conquer, open state a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: As prince, Li Shou was studious and respectful of talent, pored over stories of generals and ministers who built lasting achievement, and so won victories on every front and expanded his domain for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 雄既垂心于上，壽亦盡誠於下，號為賢相。

translations.literal: Xiong already hung heart above; Shou also exhausted sincerity below; was called worthy chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong watched over him from the throne while he served with utter loyalty below—men called him an exemplary minister.

sentences.zh: 及即偽位之後，改立宗廟，以父驤為漢始祖廟，特、雄為大成廟，又下書言與期、越別族，凡諸制度，皆有改易。

translations.literal: When he reached the false position afterward, he changed and established ancestral temple; took father Xiang as Han First Ancestor temple, Te and Xiong as Dacheng temple; again issued document saying with Qi, Yue separate clans; all various institutions all had changes.
translations.idiomatic: After usurping the throne he rebuilt the ancestral shrines—one for Li Xiang as primogenitor of “Han,” another for Li Te and Li Xiong as the “Great Accomplishment” temple—and issued edicts declaring himself unrelated to Li Qi and Li Yue, revising every major institution.

sentences.zh: 公卿以下，率用己之僚佐，雄時舊臣及六郡士人，皆見廢黜。

translations.literal: From dukes and ministers downward, generally used his own staff assistants; Xiong-time old ministers and six commanderies scholars, all were seen dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Every office below the chief ministers was filled with his own men, while Li Xiong’s veterans and gentry from the six commanderies were swept aside.

sentences.zh: 壽初病，思明等復議奉王室，壽不從。

translations.literal: When Shou first fell ill, Siming and others again deliberated serving the royal house; Shou did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his illness Xie Siming and others urged him to acknowledge Jin; Li Shou refused.

sentences.zh: 李演自越巂上書，勸壽歸正返本，釋帝稱王，壽怒殺之，以威龔壯、思明等。

translations.literal: Li Yan from Yuexi submitted memorial, urging Shou return to rectitude revert to root, release emperor title call king; Shou angrily killed him, to awe Gong Zhuang, Siming, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan of Yuexi memorialized that Li Shou should return to legitimacy, drop the imperial title, and style himself king; Li Shou executed him in fury to intimidate Gong Zhuang and Xie Siming.

sentences.zh: 壯作詩七篇，托言應璩以諷壽。

translations.literal: Zhuang composed seven poems, using the pretext of Ying Qu to satirize Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Zhuang wrote seven poems in the voice of Ying Qu to needle Li Shou.

sentences.zh: 壽報曰：「省詩知意，若今人所作，賢哲之話言也。

translations.literal: Shou replied saying, "Examining poems knows meaning; if by modern people composed, is worthy sage's discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou answered, “Reading these lines I grasp your meaning: were they written today, they would pass for the counsel of sages.”

sentences.zh: 古人所作，死鬼之常辭耳！

translations.literal: What ancients composed is dead ghosts' common phrases!
translations.idiomatic: But because they mimic the ancients, they are only the chatter of ghosts!”

sentences.zh: 」動慕漢武、魏明之所為，恥聞父兄時事，上書者不得言先世政化，自以己勝之也。

translations.literal: " He moved to admire what Han Wu and Wei Ming did; ashamed to hear father and elder brothers' era affairs; memorial submitters could not speak of former generations' government transformation; himself thought himself superior to them.
translations.idiomatic: He aped Emperor Wu of Han and Emperor Ming of Wei, shunned any talk of his father’s and uncles’ reigns, and forbade memorials that praised earlier administrations, convinced that he had surpassed them all.

sentences.zh: 李勢

translations.literal: Li Shi
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi

sentences.zh: 勢字子仁，壽之長子也。

translations.literal: Shi, courtesy name Ziren, was Shou's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi, courtesy name Ziren, was Li Shou’s eldest son.

sentences.zh: 初，壽妻閻氏無子，驤殺李鳳，為壽納鳳女，生勢。

translations.literal: Initially, Shou's wife the Lady Yan had no sons; Xiang killed Li Feng, for Shou took Feng's daughter, bore Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yan bore no children, so after Li Xiang killed Li Feng, Li Shou took Li Feng’s daughter as a concubine and she gave birth to Li Shi.

sentences.zh: 期愛勢姿貌，拜翊軍將軍、漢王世子。

translations.literal: Qi loved Shi's bearing and looks, appointed General Who Aids the Army, Han Prince heir.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi admired his looks and named him general who aids the army and heir apparent to the Han princedom.

sentences.zh: 勢身長七尺九寸，腰帶十四圍，善於俯仰，時人異之。

translations.literal: Shi's body was seven chi nine cun in height, waist belt fourteen wei; skilled in bending and rising; people of the time marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven chi nine cun tall with a fourteen-hand girth, moved with uncanny poise, and contemporaries thought him extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 壽死，勢嗣偽位，赦其境內，改元曰太和。

translations.literal: When Shou died, Shi succeeded false position, amnestied his territory, changed era to Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shou died, Li Shi succeeded him, proclaimed an amnesty, and adopted the reign title Taihe.

sentences.zh: 尊母閻氏為太后，妻李氏為皇后。

translations.literal: He honored mother the Lady Yan as empress dowager, wife the Lady Li as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He elevated Lady Yan to empress dowager and invested Lady Li as empress.

sentences.zh: 太史令韓皓奏熒惑守心，以過廟禮廢，勢命群臣議之。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Han Hao memorialized Mars guarding the heart, because excessive temple rites were abandoned; Shi ordered the host of ministers to deliberate it.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hao, the grand astrologer, reported that Mars had lodged in the “heart” mansion—a sign that ancestral rites had been neglected—so Li Shi ordered a court debate.

sentences.zh: 其相國董皎、侍中王嘏等以為景武昌業，獻文承基，至親不遠，無宜疏絕。

translations.literal: His Chancellor of State Dong Jiao, Palace Attendant Wang Gu and others thought Jing-Wu accomplished enterprise, Xian-Wen inherited foundation; utmost kin not distant—there should be no reason to sever.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Dong Jiao and Wang Gu argued that the “Jing and Wu” founders had laid the enterprise, while the “Xian and Wen” line had inherited it—close kin should not be cast off.

sentences.zh: 勢更令祭特、雄，同號曰漢王。

translations.literal: Shi further ordered sacrifice to Te, Xiong, together styled King of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi therefore restored sacrifices to Li Te and Li Xiong, honoring both as kings of Han.

sentences.zh: 勢弟大將軍、漢王廣以勢無子，求為太弟，勢弗許。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Grand General, Han King Guang because Shi had no sons, requested to be supreme younger brother; Shi did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Li Guang, grand general and prince of Han, asked to be named heir presumptive because Li Shi had no son; Li Shi refused.

sentences.zh: 馬當、解思明以勢兄弟不多，若有所廢，則益孤危，固勸許之。

translations.literal: Ma Dang, Xie Siming because Shi's brothers were not many, if there were deposition, then increased isolation and peril, firmly urged permitting it.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Dang and Xie Siming, noting how few brothers Li Shi had, warned that deposing Li Guang would isolate the throne and pressed him to agree.

sentences.zh: 勢疑當等與廣有謀，遣其太保李奕襲廣於涪城，命董皎收馬當、思明斬之，夷其三族。

translations.literal: Shi suspected Dang and others with Guang had plot; sent his Grand Guardian Li Yi to raid Guang at Fucheng, ordered Dong Jiao to seize Ma Dang, Siming, behead them, exterminate their three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting Ma Dang and Xie Siming of colluding with Li Guang, he sent Grand Guardian Li Yi against Li Guang at Fu and ordered Dong Jiao to arrest Ma Dang and Xie Siming, execute them, and wipe out their kin to the third degree.

sentences.zh: 貶廣為臨邛侯，廣自殺。

translations.literal: He demoted Guang to Marquis of Linqiong; Guang killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang was demoted to marquis of Linqiong and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 思明有計謀，強諫諍，馬當甚得人心。

translations.literal: Siming had stratagems, strongly remonstrated; Ma Dang greatly won people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Siming was a strategist who spoke bluntly, and Ma Dang was beloved by the people.

sentences.zh: 自此之後，無復紀綱及諫諍者。

translations.literal: From this afterward, no more guiding principles and remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: After their deaths no discipline remained and no one dared remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 李奕自晉壽舉兵反之，蜀人多有從奕者，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: Li Yi from Jinshou raised troops to rebel against him; Shu people many had followers of Yi; the host reached several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi rose at Jinshou against him, and tens of thousands of Shu men rallied to his banner.

sentences.zh: 勢登城距戰。

translations.literal: Shi ascended the wall to resist battle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi mounted the walls to fight them off.

sentences.zh: 奕單騎突門，門者射而殺之，眾乃潰散。

translations.literal: Yi alone on horse burst the gate; gate guards shot and killed him; the host thereupon scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi charged the gate alone; the guards shot him down, and his army melted away.

sentences.zh: 勢既誅奕，大赦境內，改年嘉寧。

translations.literal: When Shi had executed Yi, he greatly amnestied within the territory, changed year to Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: After executing Li Yi he declared a general amnesty and adopted the reign title Jianning.

sentences.zh: 初，蜀土無獠，至此，始從山而出，北至犍為，梓潼，布在山谷，十餘萬落，不可禁制，大為百姓之患。

translations.literal: Initially, Shu land had no Liao; coming to here, they first from mountains came out, north to Qianwei, Zitong, spread in mountain valleys, more than hundred thousand settlements, could not be forbidden and controlled, greatly became the hundred surnames' calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly there had been no Liao peoples in Shu; now they poured from the hills north into Qianwei and Zitong until more than a hundred thousand hamlets dotted the valleys—beyond government control and a scourge to the farmers.

sentences.zh: 勢既驕吝，而性愛財色，常殺人而取其妻，荒淫不恤國事。

translations.literal: Shi was both arrogant and stingy; and his nature loved wealth and sex; often killed people and took their wives; dissolute without caring for state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi grew arrogant and miserly, craved wealth and women, routinely murdered men to seize their wives, and abandoned statecraft to debauchery.

sentences.zh: 夷獠叛亂，軍守離缺，境宇日蹙。

translations.literal: Yi and Liao rebelled and were in chaos; army garrisons scattered and lacked; border domain daily pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes and Liao raiders revolted, garrisons stood empty, and the realm shrank by the day.

sentences.zh: 加之荒儉，性多忌害，誅殘大臣，刑獄濫加，人懷危懼。

translations.literal: Added to famine and austerity; nature much jealous harm; executed and mutilated great ministers; punishments and prisons excessively applied; people harbored peril and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Famine compounded his suspicious cruelty: he butchered senior ministers, filled the prisons on whim, and everyone walked in terror.

sentences.zh: 斥外父祖臣佐，親任左右小人，群小因行威福。

translations.literal: He pushed away outer father and grandfather ministers and assistants; personally trusted left and right petty men; the crowd of petty men thereby exercised might and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: He cast off his father’s and grandfather’s advisers, trusted petty favorites at his elbow, and let them wield arbitrary power.

sentences.zh: 又常居內，少見公卿。

translations.literal: Again he constantly dwelt within, rarely saw dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He rarely emerged from the harem and seldom received his high ministers.

sentences.zh: 史官屢陳災譴，乃加董皎太師，以名位優之，實欲與分災眚。

translations.literal: Historians repeatedly presented disaster reproofs; thereupon added Dong Jiao Grand Preceptor, by name and rank honored him; in truth wished to share calamity and ill-omen with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the historians kept citing omens, he named Dong Jiao grand preceptor—a hollow honor meant to shift cosmic blame onto him.

sentences.zh: 大司馬桓溫率水軍伐勢。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Huan Wen led naval forces to campaign against Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand marshal Huan Wen led a riverine force against Li Shi.

sentences.zh: 溫次青衣，勢大發軍距守，又遣李福與昝堅等數千人從山陽趣合水距溫。

translations.literal: Wen halted at Qingyi; Shi greatly issued troops to resist and hold; again sent Li Fu with Zan Jian and others several thousand men from Shanyang hastening to Heshui to resist Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen stopped at Qingyi; Li Shi mustered his army for defense and sent Li Fu, Zan Jian, and several thousand men from Shanyang toward Heshui to block him.

sentences.zh: 謂溫從步道而上，諸將皆欲設伏於江南以待王師，昝堅不從，率諸軍從江北鴛鴦碕渡向犍為，而溫從山陽出江南，昝堅到犍為，方知與溫異道，乃回從沙頭津北渡。

translations.literal: They thought Wen would go by foot paths upward; the generals all wished to set ambush south of the river to await the royal army; Zan Jian did not follow, led various armies from north of the river Yuanyangqi ford toward Qianwei, but Wen from Shanyang emerged south of the river; when Zan Jian reached Qianwei, then knew he was on a different route from Wen; thereupon returned from Shatou Ford to cross north.
translations.idiomatic: Expecting Huan Wen to march overland, Li Shi’s generals wanted ambushes south of the Yangzi; Zan Jian refused, crossed at Yuanyangqi on the north bank toward Qianwei, while Huan Wen emerged on the south bank from Shanyang. Reaching Qianwei too late, Zan Jian doubled back to cross north at Shatou ford.

sentences.zh: 及堅至，溫已造成都之十里陌，昝堅眾自潰。

translations.literal: When Jian arrived, Wen had already reached Chengdu's ten-li paths; Zan Jian's host spontaneously collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Zan Jian arrived, Huan Wen was already at the outskirts of Chengdu; Zan’s men broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 溫至城下，縱火燒其大城諸門。

translations.literal: Wen reached below the wall, released fire burning the great city's various gates.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen reached the walls and set fire to the main gates.

sentences.zh: 勢眾惶懼，無復固志，其中書監王嘏、散騎常侍常璩等勸勢降。

translations.literal: Shi's host fearful and afraid, no more firm resolve; among them Palace Secretary Wang Gu, Cavalier Attendant Chang Qu and others urged Shi to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi’s troops panicked and lost heart; Wang Gu, Chang Qu, and others urged him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 勢以問侍中馮孚，孚言：「昔吳漢征蜀，盡誅公孫氏。

translations.literal: Shi thereby asked Palace Attendant Feng Fu; Fu said, "Formerly Wu Han campaigned against Shu, entirely executed the Gongsun clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi consulted Feng Fu, who answered, “When Wu Han conquered Shu he exterminated the house of Gongsun.

sentences.zh: 今晉下書，不赦諸李，雖降，恐無全理。

translations.literal: Now Jin issued documents, not amnestying the various Li; although surrender, fear there is no whole-preserving principle.
translations.idiomatic: Jin has issued orders not to spare the Li clan; surrender may not save us.”

sentences.zh: 」勢乃夜出東門，與昝堅走至晉壽，然後送降文于溫曰：「偽三月十七日，略陽李勢叩頭死罪。

translations.literal: " Shi thereupon by night exited east gate, with Zan Jian fled to Jinshou, then sent surrender document to Wen saying, "False third month seventeenth day, Lüeyang Li Shi knocks head capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi slipped out the east gate with Zan Jian and fled to Jinshou, then sent Huan Wen a letter of surrender: “On the seventeenth day of the third month, Li Shi of Lüeyang prostrates himself in capital guilt.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大將軍節下，先人播流，恃險因釁，竊自汶、蜀。

translations.literal: I prostrate thinking Grand General beneath your command: former men scattered drifting, relied on peril and seized opportunity, stole from Wen and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Great General, my forebears were cast about by chaos, seized the mountain barriers, and carved out a realm between Wen and Shu.”

sentences.zh: 勢以暗弱，復統未緒，偷安荏苒，未能改圖。

translations.literal: Shi by dim weakness, again inheriting uncontinued thread, stole peace drifting, was unable to change plans.
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and feeble, inherited a broken line, clung to precarious peace, and failed to mend our course.”

sentences.zh: 猥煩硃軒，踐冒險阻。

translations.literal: Vulgarly troubling vermilion carriage, treading and braving peril and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: We have troubled your vermilion chariot to cross these treacherous roads.

sentences.zh: 將士狂愚，干犯天威。

translations.literal: Generals and soldiers mad and foolish, offending Heaven's majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Our soldiers, rash and blind, have offended the majesty of the throne.

sentences.zh: 仰慚俯愧，精魂飛散，甘受斧鑕，以釁軍鼓。

translations.literal: Looking up ashamed, looking down ashamed; essence-soul flies and scatters; willingly accept axe and chopping-block, to smear the battle drums.
translations.idiomatic: Shame consumes us body and soul; we are willing to die beneath the axe and let our blood consecrate the army drums.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大晉，天網恢弘，澤及四海，恩過陽日。

translations.literal: I prostrate thinking great Jin: Heaven's net vast and great, moisture reaches four seas, grace surpasses the yang sun.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin casts its net wide, its kindness floods the four seas, and its mercy outshines the sun.

sentences.zh: 逼迫倉卒，自投草野。

translations.literal: Pressed and rushed, myself cast into grass and wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed and in haste, I have fled into the wilderness.

sentences.zh: 即日到白水城，謹遣私署散騎常侍王幼奉箋以聞，並敕州郡投戈釋杖。

translations.literal: This day arrived at Baishui city; respectfully send privately appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Wang You bearing document to report, and together order commanderies to cast spears and release staves.
translations.idiomatic: This day I reached Baishui and dispatch Wang You, whom I had named cavalier attendant, to present this petition; I have ordered every district to lay down arms.

sentences.zh: 窮池之魚，待命漏刻。

translations.literal: Fish in an exhausted pool, awaiting fate in clepsydra moments.
translations.idiomatic: We are fish in a drying pool, waiting breathless moment by moment for your decree.

sentences.zh: 」勢尋輿櫬面縛軍門，溫解其縛，焚其櫬，遷勢及弟福、從兄權親族十餘人于健康，封勢歸義侯。

translations.literal: Shi soon came with a coffin cart, his hands bound at the camp gate; Wen released his bonds, burned the bier cart, moved Shi and younger brother Fu, cousin Quan, and more than ten kinsmen to Jiankang, enfeoffed Shi as Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Shi appeared at the camp gate with a coffin cart, hands bound; Huan Wen freed him, burned the cart, and resettled Li Shi, his brother Li Fu, his cousin Li Quan, and more than ten kinsmen at the Eastern Jin capital Jiankang, enfeoffing him as marquis of returning allegiance.

sentences.zh: ，死于建康。

translations.literal: , died at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 在位五年而敗。

translations.literal: On the throne five years then defeated.
translations.idiomatic: His reign lasted five years before collapse.

sentences.zh: 始，李特以惠帝起兵，至此六世，凡四十六年，以穆帝滅。

translations.literal: From the beginning, Li Te with Emperor Hui raised troops; coming to here six generations; altogether forty-six years; by Emperor Mu extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: From Li Te’s uprising under Emperor Hui of Jin through six generations and forty-six years, the line ended with Emperor Mu.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historical appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historians’ Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔周德方隆，古公切逾梁之患；

translations.literal: The historian says: Formerly Zhou virtue was just rising; Ancient Duke urgently crossed the peril of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: When Zhou’s power was waxing, the ancient duke still had to flee the peril at Mount Liang;

sentences.zh: 漢祚斯永，宣後興渡湟之師。

translations.literal: Han mandate thus long; Empress Xuan raised the army that crossed the Huang.
translations.idiomatic: when Han’s mandate seemed secure, Empress Xuan still had to launch the host that crossed the Huang River.

sentences.zh: 是知戎狄亂華，釁深自古，況乎巴、濮雜種，厥類實繁，資剽竊以全生，習獷悍而成俗。

translations.literal: From this know Rong and Di disorder Huaxia; rancor is deep from antiquity—how much more for Ba and Pu mixed breeds, their kinds truly numerous, relying on pillage and theft to preserve life, practicing fierce boldness until it becomes custom.
translations.idiomatic: So we know northern tribes have vexed the Central Plains since ancient times; the Ba and Pu admixtures are more numerous still, living by plunder and hardened into savagery.

sentences.zh: 李特世傳凶狡，早擅梟雄，太息劍門，志吞井絡。

translations.literal: Li Te for generations transmitted fierce cunning; early monopolized fierce champion; great sigh at Sword Gate; ambition to swallow the Well Net.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the Li clan bred cunning; Li Te was a born warlord who brooded at Jianmen Gorge and meant to devour the Shu basin.

sentences.zh: 屬晉綱之落紐，乘羅侯之無斷，騁馬屬犍，同聲雲集，殲殄蜀、漢，薦食巴、梁，沃野無半菽之資，華陽有析骸之釁。

translations.literal: Just when Jin guiding rope dropped its knot, riding Marquis Luo's lack of decision, galloping horses linked to Qian, same voice cloud-gathered, exterminated Shu and Han, silkworm-ate Ba and Liang; fertile fields had not half-bean resources; Huayang had split-bones rancor.
translations.idiomatic: As Jin’s grip slackened and Luo Shang hesitated, Li Te’s riders poured through Qianwei; allies flocked to him, Shu and Han were crushed, Ba and Liang gnawed away until the fertile plain could not spare half a bean and Huayang knew the famine where kin broke bones for fuel.

sentences.zh: 蓋上失其道，覆敗之至於斯！

translations.literal: Covering: superiors lost their Way; overturn-defeat reached to this!
translations.idiomatic: When those above abandon the Way, ruin this complete is the inevitable price.

sentences.zh: 仲俊天挺英姿，見稱奇偉，摧鋒累載，克隆霸業。

translations.literal: Zhongjun Heaven-raised heroic bearing, seen praised as marvelous and great; crushed spear-points accumulated years; greatly cloned hegemon enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjun—Li Xiong—was heaven’s favorite, hailed as a marvel; year after year he broke enemy lines and built a lasting hegemony.

sentences.zh: 蹈玄德之前基，掩子陽之故地，薄賦而綏弊俗，約法而悅新邦，擬於其倫，實孫權之亞也。

translations.literal: Trod Xuande's former foundation, covered Ziyang's old territory; light levies and pacified worn custom; restrained laws and pleased new state; compared to their class, truly Sun Quan's second.
translations.idiomatic: He trod the ground Liu Bei had held, overlaid Gongsun Shu’s old domain, eased taxes to soothe a weary people, and simplified laws until the new state rejoiced—among his peers he ranks just below Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 若夫立子以嫡，往哲通訓，繼體承基，前修茂範。

translations.literal: As for establishing sons by the legitimate heir, past sages' common teaching; inheriting body receiving foundation, former cultivated splendid model.
translations.idiomatic: Investing the legitimate heir is the lesson of every sage; succession on that pattern is the finest precedent of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 而雄暗經國之遠圖，蹈匹夫之小節，傳大統於猶子。

translations.literal: But Xiong was dark to governing-the-state's far plan; trod common man's small restraint; transmitted great mandate to nephew-son.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Xiong ignored the long view of statecraft, clung to private sentiment, and handed the great mandate to a nephew.

sentences.zh: 托強兵於厥胤。

translations.literal: Entrusted strong troops to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: He left seasoned armies in the hands of his own sons.

sentences.zh: 遺骸莫斂，尋戈之釁已深；

translations.literal: Left bones none gathered; seeking-spear rancor already deep;
translations.idiomatic: His corpse was hardly laid to rest before the blades of kinsmen were drawn;

sentences.zh: 星紀未周，傾巢之釁便及。

translations.literal: Star-mark not yet full cycle; overturn-nest rancor then reached.
translations.idiomatic: before a full turn of the heavens the whole nest was overturned.

sentences.zh: 雖云天道，抑亦人謀。

translations.literal: Although called Heaven's Way, yet also human plotting.
translations.idiomatic: Call it fate if you will—human folly shares the blame.

sentences.zh: 班以寬愛罹災，期以暴戾速禍，殊塗並失，異術同亡。

translations.literal: Ban by lenient love met disaster; Qi by violent cruelty hastened calamity; different roads together lost; different arts together perished.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ban’s kindness brought disaster, Li Qi’s cruelty hastened ruin—opposite paths, the same end.

sentences.zh: 武考憑藉世資，窮兵竊位，罪百周帶，毒甚楚圍，獲保歸全，何其幸也！

translations.literal: Wukao relied on generation capital, exhausted troops usurped position; crimes hundred Zhou Dai; poison exceeded Chu siege; obtained protection and returned whole—how his fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Li Shou rode his father’s prestige to usurp the throne by force—guilt piled higher than the worst Zhou tyrants, cruelty worse than Chu's sieges—yet he died in his bed: what luck!

sentences.zh: 子仁承緒，繼傳昏虐，驅率餘燼，敢距大邦。

translations.literal: Ziren inherited thread; continued transmitting dark cruelty; drove and led remaining embers; dared resist great state.
translations.idiomatic: Ziren inherited the line, added folly and cruelty, and dared pit the embers of Shu against a great power.

sentences.zh: 授甲晨征，則理均於困獸；

translations.literal: Grant armor morning campaign—then principle equals cornered beast;
translations.idiomatic: Had he marched at dawn in full armor, he would only have been a cornered beast;

sentences.zh: 斬關宵遁，則義殊於前禽。

translations.literal: Cut passes night flee—then righteousness differs from former quarry.
translations.idiomatic: slipping the walls by night put him beneath even the quarry spared once before.

sentences.zh: 宜其懸首國門，以明大戮，遂得禮同劉禪，不亦優乎！

translations.literal: Fitting that hang heads at state gate, to clarify great execution; yet obtained rites same as Liu Shan—is it not generous!
translations.idiomatic: He deserved to have his head posted at the capital gate; instead he was treated like Liu Shan of Shu—could mercy go further?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：晉圖馳馭，百六斯鐘。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Jin chart gallops reins; hundred-six thus strikes.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: The Jin house raced its chariot into the “hundred and sixth” cycle of calamity.

sentences.zh: 天垂伏鱉，野戰群龍。

translations.literal: Heaven hung submitting turtle; wild battle many dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven showed the omen of the submissive tortoise; in the fields dragons warred among themselves.

sentences.zh: 李特窺釁，盜我巴、庸。

translations.literal: Li Te spied rift; stole our Ba and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te seized his chance and stole Ba and Yong from Jin.

sentences.zh: 世歷五朝，年將四紀。

translations.literal: Generations passed five courts; years approached four ji.
translations.idiomatic: Five reigns they lasted, nearly forty-eight years.

sentences.zh: 篡殺移國，昏狂繼軌。

translations.literal: Usurp kill shift state; dark mad succeed tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Usurpation and murder moved the throne from hand to hand; folly and frenzy ran in an unbroken line.

sentences.zh: 德之不修，險亦難恃。

translations.literal: Of virtue not cultivating; peril also hard to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Without cultivating virtue, not even mountains can save you.
